boundary_rationale: The book opens on a disjunctive circumstantial clause — fronted subject והמלך דוד זקן בא בימים (oshb:1Kgs.1.1) — and closes on a matching disjunctive, והמלך לא ידעה (oshb:1Kgs.1.4); the frame, not the interior, sets the unit's edges. Between those two verbless openers the report itself runs as an ordinary wayyiqtol sequence — 1:1's own וַיְכַסֻהוּ and the six further wayyiqtols of 1:2-4 (וַיֹּאמְרוּ, וַיְבַקְשׁוּ, וַיִּמְצְאוּ, וַיָבִאוּ, וַתְּהִי, וַתְּשָׁרְתֵהוּ) — narrate the search for and installation of Abishag as ordinary event sequence, not durative background. The exposition closes at web:1Kgs.1.4 on the narrator's pointed evaluation 'the king didn't know her intimately', after which 1:5 pivots to a different fronted participant entirely (ואדניה בן חגית).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 1:1-4 into the Adonijah unit as scene-setting for the succession crisis — rejected because 1:5 opens with its own disjunctive participant introduction (ואדניה בן־חגית) and a change of topic from the king's chamber to public self-exaltation; the prologue's function (the vacuum of royal vigor) is background to the whole chapter, not to Adonijah's feast alone.

boundary_rationale: A second disjunctive participant introduction — ואדניהּ בן־חגית מתנשא, fronted subject plus participial self-exaltation 'I will be king' (oshb:1Kgs.1.5) — opens the pretender unit; narrator background on David's indulgence and Adonijah's birth order (web:1Kgs.1.6) sits inside it as an off-storyline aside. The unit runs through the partisan rosters (1:7-8) to the sacrificial feast at En Rogel and closes on the pointed exclusion list at web:1Kgs.1.10: 'he didn't call Nathan... and Solomon his brother' — the omission that triggers everything that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 1:9 where the feast begins (ויזבח אדניהו, a fresh wayyiqtol chain at oshb:1Kgs.1.9) — rejected because 1:9-10 completes the conspiracy exposition begun at 1:5: the invitation and exclusion lists mirror the adherent and non-adherent rosters of 1:7-8, and no participant, place, or discourse frame intervenes between preparation and feast.

boundary_rationale: A speech formula with two newly paired participants — ויאמר נתן אל בת־שבע (oshb:1Kgs.1.11) — moves the action from Adonijah's feast to Nathan's private counsel with Bathsheba. The scene is a single plan-hatching speech (the news report 1:11, the counsel 1:12, the scripted petition 1:13, and the promised corroborating entrance 1:14) and ends exactly where its own script says the next scene will begin: 'while you are still talking there with the king, I will also come in after you and confirm your words' (web:1Kgs.1.14).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 1:11-14 into the following audience as one Nathan-orchestrated movement — rejected since the location and audience change at 1:15 (Bathsheba enters the king's chamber, ותבא בת־שבע אל־המלך החדרה at oshb:1Kgs.1.15) is a hard scene edge; the plan and its execution are distinct narrative moments, and the execution scene re-frames the participants under David's presence.

boundary_rationale: The chamber-entry formula ותבא בת־שבע אל־המלך החדרה (oshb:1Kgs.1.15) opens one continuous royal audience executed as scripted in 1:14: Bathsheba's petition (web:1Kgs.1.17-21) is still in the air when Nathan's arrival at web:1Kgs.1.22 echoes the plan rather than repeating it — the narrator recasts 1:14's first-person promise עודך...ואני אבוא אחריך into third-person narration at 1:22, והנה עודנה מדברת עם המלך ונתן הנביא בא, shifting the pronoun (עודך→עודנה), dropping the locative שם, and replacing Nathan's own first-person pledge with narrated third-person arrival — so the second entrance is internal choreography of the same audience recast in narration, not a fresh scene and not a verbatim fulfillment either. The unit closes on Nathan's clinching question at web:1Kgs.1.27; a setumah follows 1:27 in the WLC apparatus (single-witness), which under the Prophets tier lends only weak agreement to a boundary the discourse structure already sets.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 1:22 on the participant-arrival formula — normally a unit opener in this campaign — rejected here because the arrival is the narrated recasting of the plan quoted at 1:14 inside an unbroken temporal frame ('while she was still talking'); severing it would place the planned petition and its planned corroboration in different units against the text's own binding device.

boundary_rationale: David's answer-and-summons — ויען המלך דוד ויאמר קראו־לי לבת־שבע (oshb:1Kgs.1.28) — re-stages the audience: Bathsheba, who had withdrawn during Nathan's speech, is recalled and stands before the king. The unit is the royal oath itself (the חי־יהוה vow of web:1Kgs.1.29-30 resolving the sworn promise both petitioners quoted) and closes with Bathsheba's prostration and acclamation 'Let my lord King David live forever' at web:1Kgs.1.31, where the WLC places a petuchah (single-witness; weak-tier corroboration only under the parashah-in-Prophets rule).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 1:28-31 as the tail of the double audience of 1:15-27 — rejected because the summons formula at 1:28 marks a formal re-entrance (she 'came into the king's presence' afresh), the speech direction reverses from petition to decree, and the oath constitutes the audience's juridical outcome rather than another petitioning turn.

boundary_rationale: The same summons formula that restaged 1:28 now recurs with a new addressee set — ויאמר המלך דוד קראו־לי לצדוק הכהן ולנתן הנביא ולבניהו (oshb:1Kgs.1.32) — convening the loyalist triumvirate for the counter-coup. The commission specifies mule, Gihon, anointing, trumpet, and acclamation (web:1Kgs.1.33-35), and the unit closes with Benaiah's single 'Amen' acclamation (web:1Kgs.1.36, oshb:1Kgs.1.36's sole אמן) capped by the כאשר...כן comparison wishing Solomon's throne greater than David's (web:1Kgs.1.37), the last speech before the order is executed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the commission together with its execution in 1:38-40 as one anointing sequence — rejected because 1:38 shifts from direct discourse to a wayyiqtol action chain with a full cast list on the move (וירד צדוק... at oshb:1Kgs.1.38); instruction and performance are set side by side so the reader can verify point-for-point compliance, a doubling this campaign keeps as two units when the mode switches from speech to enactment.

boundary_rationale: A movement chain opens the enactment — Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, Cherethites and Pelethites 'went down' (וירד at oshb:1Kgs.1.38) — and the report executes the commission of 1:33-35 item by item: mule, Gihon, horn of oil, trumpet, acclamation (web:1Kgs.1.38-39). It crests at web:1Kgs.1.40 with the earth-splitting celebration, the acoustic event on which the next scene turns, and stops before the hearing formula that transfers the narrative to Adonijah's feast.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through 1:41-48 because the trumpet sound bridges both scenes — rejected: וישמע אדניהו at oshb:1Kgs.1.41 is a hearing formula switching location, participants, and point of view (from the procession to the feast at En Rogel); sound carrying across a cut is the device's point, not evidence of unit continuity.

boundary_rationale: The hearing formula וישמע אדניהו וכל־הקראים אשר אתו (oshb:1Kgs.1.41) relocates the narrative to the rival feast just as it ends. One interruption scene follows: Joab's question about the uproar, Jonathan's arrival ('While he yet spoke, behold...' web:1Kgs.1.42 — an arrival inside the scene's own temporal frame, matching the 1:22 pattern), and Jonathan's comprehensive report of anointing, enthronement, and David's bedside blessing (web:1Kgs.1.43-48). The scene closes at web:1Kgs.1.49 as the same הקראים who heard at 1:41 tremble, rise, and scatter — arrival-to-dispersal forming the unit's envelope.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending at 1:48 and attaching the dispersal verse to the asylum scene — rejected because 1:49's subject is still 'all the guests of Adonijah' (the feast cast introduced at 1:41), whereas 1:50 turns on a disjunctive fronted ואדניהו ירא to follow the pretender alone; the guest-list envelope binds 49 to the feast, not to the altar.

boundary_rationale: A fronted-subject disjunctive isolates the pretender — ואדניהו ירא מפני שלמה (oshb:1Kgs.1.50) — and the action moves to a new location, the altar horns. The scene runs report (web:1Kgs.1.51), Solomon's conditional clemency formula 'if he shows himself a worthy man... but if wickedness is found in him' (web:1Kgs.1.52), and dismissal 'Go to your house' (web:1Kgs.1.53), which both closes the chapter's crisis and plants the probation the Abishag affair will violate in ch. 2. The WLC sets a petuchah after 1:53 (single-witness), consonant with — though never the driver of — the close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Binding 1:50-53 with 2:13-25 as one Adonijah-downfall arc — rejected because David's testament and death (2:1-12) stand between them with their own approaching-death opening formula; the probation-violation link is a cross-unit echo (the kind recorded as a relation, not a merge).

boundary_rationale: The approaching-death formula ויקרבו ימי־דוד למות (oshb:1Kgs.2.1) opens a deathbed testament in the patriarchal mold: the Torah exhortation with its dynastic conditional (web:1Kgs.2.2-4), then three named estate items — Joab's blood-guilt (2:5-6), Barzillai's sons' table rights (2:7), Shimei's suspended oath (2:8-9). The charge ends with the last item's grim instruction at web:1Kgs.2.9, immediately before the death notice. A setumah stands after 2:6 in the WLC (single-witness): at most a weak echo of the testament's internal itemization, which this row keeps whole per the list-member principle.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the pious exhortation 2:2-4 from the political instructions 2:5-9 as different registers — rejected because the whole speech sits inside one quotation frame opened by ויצו... לאמר at 2:1, with the successive items linked by וגם and connective ו rather than by new speech formulas; register variation inside a single testament is the genre's signature, not a seam.

boundary_rationale: The register switches from scene to annal: the sleeping-with-the-fathers formula וישכב דוד עם־אבתיו (oshb:1Kgs.2.10, behind a WLC petuchah at 2:10, single-witness — weak-tier agreement only) with burial notice, the forty-year reign summary split seven-and-thirty-three (web:1Kgs.2.11), and the succession statement whose disjunctive fronting ושלמה ישב על־כסא דוד אביו (oshb:1Kgs.2.12) seats the new king with the evaluative close 'his kingdom was firmly established'. This is the first instance in Kings of the regnal-summary frame this book will repeat for every reign.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 2:12 to the Adonijah-petition scene as its setting — rejected because 2:12 is formulaic closure (ותכן מלכתו מאד) matching the annal register of 2:10-11, and the scene at 2:13 opens with its own arrival formula; 2:12 also forms the front bracket of the establishment inclusio that 2:46b closes, an envelope recorded as a relation rather than used to justify a mega-unit.

boundary_rationale: An arrival formula with peace-inquiry — ויבא אדניהו בן־חגית אל־בת־שבע... ותאמר השלום באך (oshb:1Kgs.2.13) — opens a discrete two-party scene: Adonijah's concession speech ('the kingdom was mine... it was his from Yahweh', web:1Kgs.2.15), the single petition for Abishag (web:1Kgs.2.17), and Bathsheba's assent 'I will speak for you to the king' (web:1Kgs.2.18), which discharges the scene's business and dispatches her to the next one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One relay unit 2:13-25 spanning petition, transmission, and execution — a genuinely strong alternative given the single plot thread — rejected because 2:19 carries a full scene apparatus of its own (movement to the throne room, royal rising and bowing, the throne set for the queen mother): location, participant set, and ceremonial register all change, and this campaign cuts on scene apparatus rather than plot continuity.

boundary_rationale: The entry formula ותבא בת־שבע אל־המלך שלמה (oshb:1Kgs.2.19) opens a throne-room audience staged with unique ceremony (the king rises, bows, seats his mother at his right). The relayed petition (web:1Kgs.2.20-21) triggers Solomon's reversal — the rhetorical 'Ask for him the kingdom also!' (web:1Kgs.2.22, after which the WLC sets a petuchah, single-witness, mid-scene — a placement this row records without granting it any boundary force), the oath by the establishing God (web:1Kgs.2.23-24), and Benaiah's dispatch and the execution notice ויפגע־בו וימת (web:1Kgs.2.25), a setumah following (single-witness). Petition, verdict, and execution complete one juridical audience.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting before 2:25 to make the execution a separate notice — rejected because 2:25 is the direct grammatical continuation of the oath's 'Adonijah shall be put to death today' (2:24): dispatch verse and death verb close the audience's speech act the way 2:34 and 2:46a close their counterparts, a pattern this book uses three times in sequence.

boundary_rationale: A fronted dative disjunctive — ולאביתר הכהן אמר המלך (oshb:1Kgs.2.26) — pivots from Adonijah to the second member of the old conspiracy without any scene apparatus: this is judgment-in-passing, not audience narrative. The two verses hold the banishment to Anathoth with its stayed death sentence (web:1Kgs.2.26) and the narrator's fulfillment notice tying the expulsion to Yahweh's word against the house of Eli at Shiloh (web:1Kgs.2.27); the fulfillment formula is this book's characteristic unit-closer, and the WLC petuchah after 2:27 (single-witness) sits where the formula already ends the unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping 2:26-27 with the Joab narrative that follows as one purge unit — rejected because 2:28 opens with its own news formula (והשמעה באה עד־יואב) and full scene apparatus (flight, altar, dialogue, execution), while 2:26-27 remains compressed royal speech plus editorial comment; genre and pacing differ even though the political program is continuous.

boundary_rationale: The news formula והשמעה באה עד־יואב (oshb:1Kgs.2.28) opens the fullest scene of the purge: Joab's flight to the Tent and the altar horns (echoing Adonijah's asylum in 1:50 — an echo, not a merge), Benaiah's balked summons and the king's 'Do as he has said' with the blood-guilt rationale invoking Abner and Amasa (web:1Kgs.2.31-33), the execution and wilderness burial (web:1Kgs.2.34), and the double replacement notice — Benaiah over the army, Zadok for Abiathar (web:1Kgs.2.35) — which resolves both this scene and the Abiathar notice before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending at 2:34 and making 2:35 a free-standing administrative notice — rejected because 2:35's appointments are the narrative consequence of precisely the two removals just narrated (Joab's death, Abiathar's expulsion) and carry no annal formula of their own; the verse functions as the purge section's settlement line, not as a new register.

boundary_rationale: A fresh legal transaction, not the summons wording alone, opens the last file of David's testament: the king addresses Shimei for the first time in this reign at oshb:1Kgs.2.36 (וישלח המלך ויקרא לשמעי), imposing the Jerusalem-residence injunction with its Kidron trigger and self-incurring blood formula (web:1Kgs.2.36-37); the identical consonantal summons recurs at oshb:1Kgs.2.42, but there it resumes an already-sentenced defendant mid-scene inside the next unit rather than opening one, so the formula by itself cannot carry the boundary the way a new-addressee, new-transaction pairing does at 2:36. Shimei's acceptance 'What you say is good' and the compliance notice 'Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days' (web:1Kgs.2.38) close the injunction on a durative settling that opens the clock the next unit's 'end of three years' will read. The WLC setumah after 2:38 (single-witness) coincides with, but does not produce, that pause.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One Shimei unit 2:36-46 from injunction to execution — rejected because ויהי מקץ שלש שנים at oshb:1Kgs.2.39 is a temporal-formula opening of the classic episode type; the durative 'many days' of 2:38 and the punctual 'at the end of three years' of 2:39 are exactly the settled-state/disruption hinge on which this corpus articulates episodes.

boundary_rationale: The temporal formula ויהי מקץ שלש שנים (oshb:1Kgs.2.39) breaks the settled state: the Gath errand after runaway slaves, the report to Solomon (web:1Kgs.2.41), the arraignment speech that re-quotes both the adjuration and Shimei's own acceptance (web:1Kgs.2.42-43), the theological sentence returning Shimei's wickedness on his head while blessing David's throne (web:1Kgs.2.44-45), and the execution (web:1Kgs.2.46a). The narrator's closure — והממלכה נכונה ביד־שלמה (web:1Kgs.2.46b) — completes the establishment envelope opened at 2:12 and seals the entire succession narrative; the WLC records no mark between 2:38 and 3:2 (single-witness); no weight is drawn from that absence, and the close rests on the כון inclusio (2:12's ותכן, 2:46's נכונה) on its own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Detaching 2:46b as a stand-alone editorial seam verse — rejected not because the clause continues the execution sentence syntactically (it does not: והממלכה נכונה ביד שלמה is a waw-fronted-subject nominal clause that breaks the ויצא/ויפגע/וימת wayyiqtol chain rather than extending it) but because the clause is a disjunctive editorial summary sharing the root כון with 2:12's ותכן, making it the inclusio's second bracket; isolating a clause-length row would still violate the campaign's minimum-unit discipline while adding no boundary information the relation record does not already capture.

boundary_rationale: Three verses of editorial stock-taking preface the Solomon cycle: the Pharaoh marriage-alliance notice, itself a punctual three-link wayyiqtol chain (ויתחתן/ויקח/ויביאה) reporting the alliance, the taking, and the bringing-in, with its building-program horizon (web:1Kgs.3.1); the restrictive רק clause on popular high-place sacrifice — a durative disjunctive, 'because there was not yet a house built for Yahweh's name' (oshb:1Kgs.3.2); and the programmatic evaluation 'Solomon loved Yahweh... except that he sacrificed... in the high places' (web:1Kgs.3.3) — a wayyiqtol opening (ויאהב שלמה את יהוה) whose second clause narrows, in its own רק disjunctive (רק בבמות הוא מזבח ומקטיר), to the high-place exception. None of the three carries dialogue, an interacting cast, or a located action — even 3:1's wayyiqtols report a completed state of affairs rather than staging a scene — so the whole span remains narrator assessment framing everything through ch. 11. The WLC's petuchah after 3:2 (single-witness) falls mid-preface and receives no boundary weight under the weak Prophets tier; the unit's edge is set by 3:4's movement formula instead.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 3:1-3 to the Gibeon incubation as its cultic motivation — rejected because 3:4 opens with a punctual itinerary formula (וילך המלך גבענה at oshb:1Kgs.3.4), and while 3:1 is itself punctual in form, 3:1-3 as a whole stages no scene at all: 3:2-3 pivot into the durative-evaluative רק disjunctives that actually characterize the preface, and none of the three verses supplies dialogue, a participant apparatus, or a locale of action the way 3:4's journey does; the high-place comment explains an era, not one journey.

boundary_rationale: The journey-to-sanctuary formula וילך המלך גבענה לזבח שם (oshb:1Kgs.3.4) opens the incubation account, and the vision is formally framed: 'Yahweh appeared to Solomon in a dream by night' (web:1Kgs.3.5, בחלום הלילה) opens it, and the waking notice with its editorial wink — ויקץ שלמה והנה חלום, 'Solomon awoke; and behold, it was a dream' (oshb:1Kgs.3.15) — shuts it, followed in the same verse by the return to Jerusalem, the offerings before the ark, and the feast that discharge the vision cultically. The dialogue inside (petition 3:6-9, divine grant with surplus 3:10-14) consists of turns within one dream frame. The WLC petuchah after 3:15 (single-witness) coincides with, but does not create, the frame's close; the setumah after 3:14 (single-witness) merely precedes the waking verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between the sacrifice journey 3:4 and the dream 3:5-15 — rejected because the incubation type-scene binds sanctuary sacrifice to night vision at the same site ('In Gibeon' opens 3:5, resuming 3:4's destination); severing them strips the dream of its cultic occasion and the journey of any narrative point.

boundary_rationale: The archaic narrative opener אז תבאנה — 'Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king, and stood before him' (oshb:1Kgs.3.16) — is a fresh arrival formula introducing anonymous litigants and a courtroom setting. The anecdote is one juridical scene: rival testimonies (web:1Kgs.3.17-22), the king's restatement (3:23, after which the WLC oddly sets a petuchah mid-scene — single-witness, recorded and given no force), the sword test (3:24-25), the true mother's self-revealing plea (3:26), and the verdict (3:27). The narrator's panoramic close at web:1Kgs.3.28 — all Israel hears, fears, and sees 'the wisdom of God was in him' — is the anecdote's own moral, cashing out the dream's gift of a discerning heart, and ends the unit (a setumah follows, single-witness, in weak agreement).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the verdict scene at 3:24 where speech gives way to the sword action — rejected since every intervening verse keeps the same bench, litigants, and case without any temporal or spatial break; command-and-compliance inside a trial is procedure, and the campaign's turn-marker principle holds the proceeding together until judgment issues.

boundary_rationale: A summary heading — ויהי המלך שלמה מלך על־כל־ישראל (oshb:1Kgs.4.1) — introduces the administrative dossier, and the roster formula ואלה השרים אשר־לו, 'These were the princes whom he had' (web:1Kgs.4.2), lists the court: priest, scribes, recorder, army chief, officer-supervisor, king's friend, palace chief, corvée master (web:1Kgs.4.2-6). The register closes where the next roster announces its own heading at 4:7. The WLC strews setumot through this material (after 4:1, 4:2, 4:4, 4:6 — single-witness); under the weak Prophets tier and the list-member principle these punctuate entries, and following them would dice a functioning register into name-shards. Chapter 4 sits in the crosswalk's dual-citation zone: WEB 4:1-20 aligns verse-for-verse with MT 4:1-20 (both witnesses' hard counts agree), so oshb cites here carry the same numerals.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Detaching the heading 4:1 as a free-standing regnal notice — rejected because the verse supplies the antecedent for 'whom he had' in 4:2 and carries no evaluation or chronology of its own; it is the dossier's title line, not an annal member.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:1Kgs.4.1 (MT identical segment; setumah after, single-witness)

boundary_rationale: A fronted-dative heading opens the second roster — ולשלמה שנים־עשר נצבים על־כל־ישראל, 'Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel' (oshb:1Kgs.4.7) — stating the provisioning duty each entry presupposes, and ואלה שמותם 'These are their names' (web:1Kgs.4.8) launches the twelve district entries with their territorial glosses and two royal son-in-law notes (web:1Kgs.4.11, web:1Kgs.4.15). The register ends at web:1Kgs.4.19 with the Gilead entry and the summarizing remark 'he was the only officer who was in the land'. Ten setumot track individual entries in the WLC (4:7-13, 4:16-18, single-witness) — the paradigm case this campaign's weak-corroboration tier exists for: marks that articulate list-internal structure must not shred a register that functions as one administrative document. WEB and MT numbering coincide across 4:1-20 (verified hard counts), so the dual-citation rule for this chapter is satisfied by noting the identity.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the roster from its heading (4:7 vs 4:8-19) on the ואלה שמותם formula — rejected because 4:7 defines the office and rotation ('each man had to make provision for a month') that every district entry instantiates; heading and entries are one document, as with the princes register before it.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:1Kgs.4.7 (MT identical segment; ten setumot 4:7-13,4:16-18, single-witness)

boundary_rationale: A woven annal celebrates the realm: population felicity under the sand-of-the-sea simile (web:1Kgs.4.20, fronted nominal יהודה וישראל רבים at oshb:1Kgs.4.20), imperial dominion River-to-Egypt (web:1Kgs.4.21), the daily provision quota (4:22-23), the peace summary Tiphsah-to-Gaza (4:24), vine-and-fig security Dan-to-Beersheba (4:25), the stable count (4:26), and the officers' provisioning duty resumed from 4:7 (4:27-28). The members are all durative nominal or iterative notices — no scene, no plot — held together as the dossier's 'greatness of the kingdom' panel, closing where the wisdom encomium opens with its own giving-formula at 4:29. This span crosses the versification seam: WEB 4:20 = MT 4:20, but WEB 4:21-28 = MT 5:1-8 (web:1Kgs.4.21 = oshb:1Kgs.5.1 ושלמה היה מושל; web:1Kgs.4.28 = oshb:1Kgs.5.8), so every original-language citation is dual-mapped; the MT chapter division after 4:20 is versification metadata and contributes nothing to the boundary. Setumot after MT 5:5 (= WEB 4:25) and MT 5:8 (= WEB 4:28) are single-witness weak articulation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 4:21 where dominion replaces demography (and where MT begins ch. 5) — the most defensible internal seam, rejected because 4:20 and 4:21 share the same durative-annal register and the panel's alternating weave (people, dominion, provision, dominion, security, horses, provision) resists any single thematic partition; elevating the MT chapter seam would let versification metadata drive a boundary the text's register does not mark.

boundary_rationale: A divine-gift formula turns the dossier from goods to mind: ויתן אלהים חכמה לשלמה — 'God gave Solomon abundant wisdom' (web:1Kgs.4.29 = oshb:1Kgs.5.9 in MT numbering) — reprising the sand-of-the-sea simile from 4:20 in a new key. The encomium first ranks that wisdom, unnamed, against 'all the children of the east' and 'all the wisdom of Egypt' (web:1Kgs.4.30 = oshb:1Kgs.5.10), then names the individual sages it surpasses — Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda (web:1Kgs.4.31 = oshb:1Kgs.5.11) — inventories his output (three thousand proverbs, a thousand and five songs, web:1Kgs.4.32), spans his learning cedar-to-hyssop (4:33), and closes with the world's pilgrimage 'to hear the wisdom of Solomon' (web:1Kgs.4.34 = oshb:1Kgs.5.14, a setumah following in the WLC, single-witness) — the note on which the Hiram embassy of ch. 5 arrives, since Hiram 'heard'. Every oshb citation in this span maps by the WEB 4:21-34 = MT 5:1-14 rule (MT verse equals WEB verse minus twenty), not by the +14 offset that governs the adjacent WEB 5:1-18 = MT 5:15-32 block.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the encomium into the prosperity annal as one realm-panel — rejected because 4:29 opens with a fresh divine-subject giving formula and the topic pivots from provisioning economics to intellectual fame; the encomium also functions as the narrative hinge to ch. 5 (Hiram hears of the wisdom), a role the provision annal does not share.

boundary_rationale: An embassy formula opens the diplomatic file: 'Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard...' (web:1Kgs.5.1 = oshb:1Kgs.5.15 in MT numbering, וישלח חירם), the hearing motive picking up the world-audience note that closed the wisdom encomium. The transaction unfolds as paired messages — Solomon's request with its temple rationale and Sidonian-loggers compliment (web:1Kgs.5.2-6), Hiram's jubilation and counter-offer of sea rafts for household food (web:1Kgs.5.7-9) — then the exchange summary (timber for wheat and oil, year by year, web:1Kgs.5.10-11 = oshb:1Kgs.5.24-25 MT) and the treaty closure: wisdom-fulfillment notice, peace, and covenant (ויכרתו ברית שניהם, web:1Kgs.5.12 = oshb:1Kgs.5.26 MT) — the wayyiqtol that actually ratifies and terminates the exchange. The WLC's petuchah after MT 5:25 (single-witness) lands one verse shy of the closure and is recorded without boundary force; all Hebrew cites in this span are dual-mapped (+14 inside MT ch. 5).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Dividing the correspondence at 5:7 where Hiram takes over as speaker — rejected because request and reply are the two halves of one negotiation with no change of scene machinery (all of it happens by messenger), and the treaty formula at 5:12 ratifies the whole exchange; cutting at the speaker turn would apply the very turn-marker logic this campaign excludes.

boundary_rationale: A fresh royal-initiative formula — ויעל המלך שלמה מס מכל־ישראל, 'King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel' (web:1Kgs.5.13 = oshb:1Kgs.5.27 MT) — switches the file from diplomacy to labor administration: the thirty-thousand levy with its Lebanon rotation under Adoniram (web:1Kgs.5.14), the seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand quarrymen with their officer corps (web:1Kgs.5.15-16), the great-stones command (web:1Kgs.5.17), and the summary of the joint workforce — Solomon's and Hiram's builders with the Gebalites — preparing timber and stone (web:1Kgs.5.18 = oshb:1Kgs.5.32 MT, where the WLC sets a petuchah, single-witness, in weak accord with the account's end). The setumah after MT 5:28 (= WEB 5:14, single-witness) articulates the rotation entry only. Chapter 6 then restarts with the era-dating formula. Hebrew citations remain dual-mapped throughout this offset chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 5:13-18 as the tail of the treaty unit since the labor serves the same building program — rejected because 5:13 opens with its own royal-action formula and a new administrative register (numbers, rotations, supervisors) with Hiram now a third-party participant rather than a correspondent; program continuity across the seam is what the sequential dossier structure already conveys.

boundary_rationale: The grand era formula — 'In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign... in the month Ziv' (web:1Kgs.6.1, oshb:1Kgs.6.1) — anchors the temple record to exodus chronology and opens the exterior specification: overall dimensions (6:2-3), lattice windows (6:4), the three-story side chambers with their offset-beam engineering (6:5-6), the quarry-silence notice (web:1Kgs.6.7, itself a narrator aside on construction piety), the winding stairs (6:8), and the first completion-plus-roofing summary ויבן את־הבית ויכלהו (web:1Kgs.6.9-10). The WLC petuchah after 6:10 (single-witness) accords weakly with a close the next verse makes certain, since 6:11 is a word-event formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the record through 6:38 as one chapter-length building account — rejected because the divine interrupt at 6:11-13 carries the book's marked word-event formula and the account itself is articulated by the resumptive repetition of 6:9's completion clause at 6:14; a chapter-shaped row would flatten the record's own editorial joints (and would take the T423 chapter-only cap for nothing).

boundary_rationale: The word-event formula ויהי דבר־יהוה אל־שלמה לאמר (oshb:1Kgs.6.11) breaks into the specification mid-build — the only speech in chapters 6-7 — and delivers a conditional oracle on the house under construction: obedience will establish the Davidic word, and 'I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel' (web:1Kgs.6.12-13). The oracle ends where the construction record resumes at 6:14 by repeating 6:9's completion clause verbatim (ויבן... את־הבית ויכלהו) — a textbook Wiederaufnahme bracketing the insertion. The WLC setumah after 6:13 (single-witness) sits in weak agreement with the resumption seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing the oracle into the surrounding building record as a parenthesis — rejected because the word-event formula is this corpus's strongest recurring unit opener (compare 12:22, 16:1, 17:2), the register shifts from technical specification to conditional covenant speech, and the resumptive-repetition bracket shows the editor himself treating 6:11-13 as an insertable block.

boundary_rationale: The resumptive completion clause ויבן שלמה את־הבית ויכלהו (oshb:1Kgs.6.14, retaking oshb:1Kgs.6.9 after the oracle) reopens the record on a new specification front — the interior: cedar walls and cypress floor (web:1Kgs.6.15), the twenty-cubit rear partition 'for an inner sanctuary, even for the most holy place' (web:1Kgs.6.16), carved cedar with no stone visible (6:18), the debir prepared for the ark (6:19-20), and the escalating gold overlay that closes on totality — 'He overlaid the whole house with gold, until all the house was finished' (web:1Kgs.6.22). The next verse turns from surfaces to furniture with a fresh object-making formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the debir material 6:19-22 from the paneling 6:15-18 — rejected because the interior specification moves as one continuous gradient from outer hall to inner shrine to gold saturation, with no formula break: 6:19 continues the same asyndetic record style, and the gold overlay of 6:20-22 spans hall and shrine alike, welding the two topics together.

boundary_rationale: A making formula with a new object and material — ויעש בדביר שני כרובים עצי־שמן, 'In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood' (oshb:1Kgs.6.23) — opens the record's first furniture entry. The entry is a self-contained specification: wing measurements verse by verse (web:1Kgs.6.24-26, with the ten-cubit symmetry stated twice), installation with wings touching wall to wall and wing to wing (web:1Kgs.6.27), and the entry's own gold-overlay close (web:1Kgs.6.28) — the same overlay cadence that closes each stage of this record.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging the cherubim with the wall-carving material that follows because both feature cherub iconography — rejected because 6:29 pivots from free-standing furniture back to architectural surfaces with a fronted-object clause covering 'all the walls of the house around' (ואת כל־קירות הבית at oshb:1Kgs.6.29); iconographic continuity is the temple's decorative program, not a unit boundary criterion.

literature_type_guess: temple_construction_record (carving, doors, and inner court close-out)
boundary_rationale: A fronted-object clause widens the lens to every wall — 'He carved all the walls of the house around with carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, inside and outside' (web:1Kgs.6.29, ואת כל־קירות הבית at oshb:1Kgs.6.29) — and the record closes out the remaining fabric in catalogue order: gold floors (6:30), the olive-wood debir doors whose posts were sized to a fifth part of the wall (web:1Kgs.6.31-32, the disputed ordinal חמשית at oshb:1Kgs.6.31), the nave doorway with posts a fourth part of the wall and folding cypress leaves (web:1Kgs.6.33-34, רבעית at oshb:1Kgs.6.33), matching carved-and-gilded decoration (6:35), and the inner court of three stone courses and one of cedar beams (web:1Kgs.6.36) — the outermost element, ending the spatial progression from shrine walls outward.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving the two door assemblies (6:31-35) their own row apart from carving and court — rejected because the passage is a close-out sweep chained by simple waw parataxis, its items ordered spatially rather than framed individually; only the date colophon that follows carries a genuine formula change.

boundary_rationale: The record's chronological seal: two date-fronted notices carrying passive and impersonal predicates rather than the specification's own asyndetic register — 'The foundation of Yahweh's house was laid in the fourth year, in the month Ziv' (web:1Kgs.6.37, fronted בשנה הרביעית יֻסַּד at oshb:1Kgs.6.37) and 'In the eleventh year, in the month Bul... the house was finished throughout all its parts' with the closing wayyiqtol tallying seven years of building (web:1Kgs.6.38, כָלָה הבית...ויבנהו שבע שנים at oshb:1Kgs.6.38) — bracket back to the era formula of 6:1 (same fourth year, same month Ziv), closing the temple account as an annalistic envelope. The palace notice at 7:1 then opens with a contrastive fronted object (ואת־ביתו בנה שלמה, oshb:1Kgs.7.1) and its own thirteen-year figure.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the colophon to the close-out unit 6:29-36 — rejected because 6:37-38 abandons specification entirely for bare chronography, reprising 6:1's date coordinates to form the envelope; it seals the whole seven-chapter-spanning temple fabric account, not the final work items alone.

boundary_rationale: A contrastive fronted object turns the record from Yahweh's house to the king's — ואת־ביתו בנה שלמה שלש עשרה שנה, 'Solomon was building his own house thirteen years' (oshb:1Kgs.7.1) — the thirteen-year figure answering the temple's seven (6:38). The palace dossier then runs building by building: the House of the Forest of Lebanon with its pillar forest (web:1Kgs.7.2-5), the hall of pillars (7:6), the porch of judgment (7:7), the residence and the house for Pharaoh's daughter (web:1Kgs.7.8, closing the loop opened at 3:1), and the masonry summary of costly sawed stones down to the great court (web:1Kgs.7.9-12), whose cedar-course construction echoes the inner court of 6:36. The WLC petuchah after 7:12 (single-witness) weakly seconds a close that 7:13's summons formula makes anyway.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting each named building into its own row — a move once defended by calling 7:1 the span's only clause-initial framing formula, a claim direct collation disproves: oshb:1Kgs.7.6 (וְאֵת אוּלָם הָעַמּוּדִים עָשָׂה), 7.7 (וְאוּלָם הַכִּסֵּא...עָשָׂה), and 7.8 (וּבֵיתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יֵשֶׁב שָׁם...הָיָה) all open with the same fronted-constituent-plus-verb shape as 7.1. The merge instead rests on what those same verses lack: no entry inside 7:2-8 carries its own completion or closure formula (contrast the entry-closers at oshb:1Kgs.7.22 and 7.37), the buildings are chained by simple waw parataxis with no change of participant or time reference, and oshb:1Kgs.7.9's כָּל אֵלֶּה ('all these') gathers the whole set under one masonry summary rather than closing a single item.

literature_type_guess: bronze_works_craft_catalogue (artisan introduction and the two pillars)
boundary_rationale: A royal summons opens the bronze catalogue — וישלח המלך שלמה ויקח את־חירם מצר (oshb:1Kgs.7.13) — introducing the artisan Hiram with a pedigree and endowment notice in the Bezalel mold ('filled with wisdom and understanding and skill to work all works in bronze', web:1Kgs.7.14). The first catalogue entry follows: the two eighteen-cubit pillars with their capitals, networks, and pomegranate rows (web:1Kgs.7.15-20), their erection and naming — Jachin on the right, Boaz on the left (web:1Kgs.7.21) — and the entry's own completion formula, ותתם מלאכת העמודים, 'So the work of the pillars was finished' (oshb:1Kgs.7.22), the crispest internal closer in the chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the artisan introduction 7:13-14 from the pillar entry — rejected because 7:14 ends by making Hiram the subject who 'performed all his work', and 7:15's fashioning verbs continue that subject without any new frame; the introduction is the catalogue's header and travels with its first entry rather than standing as a two-verse fragment.

boundary_rationale: The object-making formula ויעש את־הים מוצק, 'He made the molten sea' (oshb:1Kgs.7.23), opens the catalogue's second entry, a compact specification: ten cubits brim to brim with the thirty-cubit line (web:1Kgs.7.23), the cast bud rows (7:24), the twelve oxen facing the four compass points with hindquarters inward (web:1Kgs.7.25), and the closing gauge — a handbreadth thick, a lily-cup brim, two thousand baths (web:1Kgs.7.26). The WLC petuchah after 7:26 (single-witness) falls exactly at the entry's natural end, where the next ויעש formula introduces the bases.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Bundling sea and bases into one basins-apparatus entry since the basins ride the bases and the sea holds water for the same cultic washing system — rejected because the catalogue's own grammar individuates entries by the ויעש formula plus object (sea at 7:23, bases at 7:27, basins at 7:38), and function-based grouping would override the document's explicit itemization.

literature_type_guess: bronze_works_craft_catalogue (the ten bases and basins with installation notice)
boundary_rationale: The formula ויעש את־המכנות עשר נחשת (oshb:1Kgs.7.27) opens the catalogue's most elaborate entry: the wheeled stands specified panel by panel — lions, oxen, and cherubim on the frames, chariot-style wheels, cast supports (web:1Kgs.7.28-36) — sealed by the uniformity colophon 'all of them had one casting, one measure, and one form' (web:1Kgs.7.37, a setumah following, single-witness). The paired basins ride the same entry (ויעש עשרה כירות at oshb:1Kgs.7.38 — forty baths each, one per stand), and the installation notice ויתן את־המכנות places stands five-and-five and positions the sea (web:1Kgs.7.39, setumah after, single-witness), closing the workshop's fabrication phase before the summary inventory.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 7:38 to give the basins and the placement verse their own row — a real option given 7:38's fresh ויעש formula — rejected because the basins are defined by their stands (dimension and count derive from them, 'one basin on every one of the ten bases'), and the placement verse disposes of stands and sea together; a two-verse row mixing fabrication and installation would fragment what functions as the entry's completion.

boundary_rationale: The small-vessels notice pivots immediately into the master completion formula — ויעש חירום את־הכירות ואת־היעים ואת־המזרקות ויכל חירם לעשות את־כל־המלאכה, 'So Hiram finished doing all the work' (oshb:1Kgs.7.40) — and the catalogue recapitulates itself as a formal inventory: pillars, capital bowls, networks, four hundred pomegranates, ten bases, ten basins, one sea, twelve oxen, and the utensils, all burnished bronze (web:1Kgs.7.41-45). Two provenance notes close the account: the Jordan-plain clay-ground casting between Succoth and Zarethan (web:1Kgs.7.46) and the unweighed-bronze notice (web:1Kgs.7.47). This is the catalogue's own colophon — a register distinct from the entries it tallies.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the inventory to the bases-and-basins entry it follows — rejected because 7:40's ויכל formula terminates the whole bronze commission (echoing the completion formulas at 6:9, 6:14, and 6:38), and the itemized recapitulation spans every entry back to 7:15; it summarizes the catalogue rather than extending its last item.

boundary_rationale: Subject and material change together: ויעש שלמה את כל־הכלים אשר בית יהוה — Solomon, not Hiram, makes the gold vessels (oshb:1Kgs.7.48): golden altar, showbread table, the five-and-five lampstands before the debir, and the utensil list down to gold door hinges (web:1Kgs.7.48-50, a petuchah after 7:50, single-witness). The grand completion then seals both chapters — ותשלם כל־המלאכה, 'Thus all the work that King Solomon did in Yahweh's house was finished' (oshb:1Kgs.7.51) — and the deposit of David's dedicated silver, gold, and vessels stocks the treasuries (web:1Kgs.7.51), placing the finished, furnished, funded house ready for the ark's entry in ch. 8. A second petuchah follows 7:51 (single-witness), where the אז יקהל assembly formula opens the dedication narrative.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 7:51 as a stand-alone completion seam — rejected because the ותשלם formula is the direct capstone of the vessel-making it follows (the same verse carries the deposit action, still inventory-handling), and the campaign's minimum-unit discipline resists one-verse editorial rows when the formula plainly closes the register it ends.

boundary_rationale: The archaic assembly opener אז יקהל שלמה את־זקני ישראל (oshb:1Kgs.8.1 — the same אז + yiqtol construction that opened 3:16) convenes elders, tribal heads, and princes for the ark's ascent at the seventh-month feast (web:1Kgs.8.1-2). The procession narrative carries ark, Tent of Meeting, and vessels upward amid uncountable sacrifices (web:1Kgs.8.4-5), installs the ark under the cherubim's wings with the poles-visible 'to this day' notice and the tablets-only inventory (web:1Kgs.8.6-9), and closes theophanically: the cloud fills the house so the priests cannot stand to minister, 'for Yahweh's glory filled Yahweh's house' (web:1Kgs.8.10-11). The WLC petuchah after 8:11 (single-witness) accords weakly with the close the glory-formula itself effects.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through Solomon's cloud-saying in 8:12-13 since it responds to the theophany — rejected because אז אמר שלמה at oshb:1Kgs.8.12 is a second archaic-formula opening that turns from third-person procession narrative to royal first-person speech; the response belongs to the address it begins, as the blessing pivot at 8:14 confirms.

boundary_rationale: אז אמר שלמה (oshb:1Kgs.8.12) opens the king's first dedication speech with the poetic dwelling-couplet — thick darkness against 'a house of habitation... forever' (web:1Kgs.8.12-13) — after which the stage direction 'The king turned his face around and blessed all the assembly' (web:1Kgs.8.14, ויסב המלך את־פניו at oshb:1Kgs.8.14) redirects the same speech-event to the people: the ברוך יהוה blessing rehearses the election of David over any chosen city (web:1Kgs.8.15-16), David's thwarted intent and the son-shall-build oracle (web:1Kgs.8.17-19), and the fulfillment claim 'I have risen up... and have built the house', with the ark's place set for the covenant (web:1Kgs.8.20-21). The WLC setumah after 8:21 (single-witness) sits where the address yields to the altar-posture formula of 8:22.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the two-verse cloud-saying from the blessing as separate speech acts — rejected because 8:14's pivot is a turn within one continuous royal speech-event (no new speaker, no scene change, the assembly present throughout), and a two-verse poetic fragment would be orphaned from the address that interprets it.

boundary_rationale: A full posture formula opens the great prayer — Solomon stands before the altar, in front of all the assembly, and spreads his hands toward heaven (web:1Kgs.8.22, ויעמד שלמה... ויפרש כפיו at oshb:1Kgs.8.22) — and a matching dismount formula closes it at 8:54 ('when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer'). Between them one liturgical composition unfolds: the incomparability invocation and Davidic petition (web:1Kgs.8.23-26), the transcendence paradox 'will God in very deed dwell on the earth?' (web:1Kgs.8.27), and the sevenfold petition series — oath at the altar, defeat, drought, famine-and-plague, the foreigner, battle, and captivity (web:1Kgs.8.31-53) — each case bound to the next by a shared hear-in-heaven refrain realized in two grammatical shapes rather than one fixed string: (וְ)אַתָּה תִּשְׁמַע הַשָּׁמַיִם at oshb:1Kgs.8.32, 8.34, 8.36, 8.39, and 8.43 (the last dropping the conjunctive vav), and וְשָׁמַעְתָּ הַשָּׁמַיִם at oshb:1Kgs.8.45 and 8.49. Both forms do the same chaining work: they articulate cases inside one prayer rather than opening units, exactly as the WLC's setumot after 8:32, 8:34, and 8:36 (single-witness) mark case-ends without unit force under the weak Prophets tier. The Egypt-separation ground clause ends the prayer at web:1Kgs.8.53, a petuchah following (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Chunking each petition as its own row on its opening particle — not, as first framed, a uniform set of אם/כי case-markers, since the seven openers actually run אֵת אֲשֶׁר (8:31), a ב-plus-infinitive-construct clause (8:33, 8:35), a bare-noun catalogue resolving into כִּי (8:37), וְגַם אֶל (8:41), and כִּי (8:44, 8:46) — rejected on the ground that survives the correction: every petition is syntactically a protasis-apodosis member of the single prayer speech within one quotation frame, sharing invocation, altar, posture, and addressee; splitting would produce seven fragments each missing the invocation that grounds them, and would follow the setumah articulation against the addendum's bar on marker-driven boundaries.

boundary_rationale: The completion formula ויהי ככלות שלמה להתפלל (oshb:1Kgs.8.54) raises the king from his knees — the dismount of 8:22's posture — and he blesses the assembly 'with a loud voice' (web:1Kgs.8.55): the rest-formula doxology 'not one word has failed of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses' (web:1Kgs.8.56), the presence petition 'as he was with our fathers' (8:57-58), the day-by-day cause-maintenance request with its universal aim 'that all the peoples of the earth may know that Yahweh himself is God' (web:1Kgs.8.59-60), and the closing exhortation to whole-hearted obedience (web:1Kgs.8.61). The benediction ends where narrative resumes with the sacrifice notice at 8:62.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the benediction into the great prayer as its coda — rejected because 8:54 is a formal boundary in the text's own words ('finished praying'), the posture changes from kneeling supplication to standing blessing, and the addressee flips from Yahweh to the assembly; the two speech-events mirror the 8:12-21 address, bracketing the prayer symmetrically.

boundary_rationale: A fronted-subject participial clause — והמלך וכל־ישראל עמו זבחים זבח לפני יהוה (oshb:1Kgs.8.62) — turns from speech to cult: the hecatomb figures (twenty-two thousand cattle, one hundred twenty thousand sheep) with the explicit dedication statement (web:1Kgs.8.63), the same-day consecration of the court's middle because the bronze altar was too small (web:1Kgs.8.64), the fourteen-day feast for a congregation spanning Hamath to the brook of Egypt (web:1Kgs.8.65, ויעש שלמה בעת־ההיא את־החג at oshb:1Kgs.8.65), and the eighth-day dismissal — the people bless the king and go to their tents 'joyful and glad in their hearts' (web:1Kgs.8.66). The dismissal formula closes the whole dedication complex; ch. 9 then opens with a fresh ויהי ככלות completion frame introducing the second theophany.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between the sacrifices (8:62-64) and the festival (8:65-66) — rejected because 8:65's 'at that time' explicitly binds the feast to the dedication occasion just narrated, and the two notices form one cultic settlement running from offering through dismissal, matching the assembly-to-dismissal envelope that 8:1-2 opened for the whole chapter.

boundary_rationale: A completion frame — ויהי ככלות שלמה לבנות, 'When Solomon had finished the building of Yahweh's house, the king's house, and all Solomon's desire' (oshb:1Kgs.9.1) — sets the occasion, and the appearance formula ties the vision explicitly to its predecessor: 'Yahweh appeared to Solomon the second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon' (web:1Kgs.9.2), forming the rear member of the dream-frame pair with 3:4-15. The oracle answers the ch. 8 prayer point for point — prayer heard, house consecrated, eyes and heart there perpetually (web:1Kgs.9.3) — then bifurcates: dynastic promise on the Davidic condition (web:1Kgs.9.4-5) against the cutting-off, the house cast from sight, and the passersby's question-and-answer etiology of ruin (web:1Kgs.9.6-9). The oracle ends with that grim antiphon; the WLC petuchah after 9:9 (single-witness) stands in weak accord with the close, and 9:10 opens on a new chronological frame.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the warning 9:6-9 from the promise 9:1-5 at the אם-clause reversal — rejected because both halves are one continuous divine speech inside a single vision frame, delivered without any change of speaker, addressee, or formula; blessing-and-curse bifurcation is simply the covenant genre's own internal shape, not a boundary marker, and the point needs no support from other passages to hold.

boundary_rationale: The chronological frame ויהי מקצה עשרים שנה — 'At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses' (oshb:1Kgs.9.10) — opens a diplomatic settlement notice: against Hiram's cedar, cypress, and gold (narrator parenthesis, web:1Kgs.9.11), Solomon cedes twenty Galilean cities; Hiram inspects, is displeased ('What cities are these..., my brother?'), and the naming etiology seals the episode — 'the land of Cabul to this day' (web:1Kgs.9.13, a petuchah following in the WLC, single-witness, mid-episode and given no force). The gold figure of one hundred twenty talents (web:1Kgs.9.14) settles the account and closes the notice before the corvée dossier's heading formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending at the etiological naming in 9:13, since naming closes elsewhere in the campaign — rejected because 9:14's payment notice is the transaction's other half (cities against gold): dropping it orphans a one-verse ledger line, and the etiology here caps the inspection dialogue rather than the whole exchange.

boundary_rationale: A document heading — וזה דבר־המס, 'This is the reason of the forced labor which King Solomon conscripted' (oshb:1Kgs.9.15) — opens the second corvée dossier (pairing with 5:13-18): the building list from the two houses through Millo, the wall, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer, with the Gezer dowry parenthesis on Pharaoh's burnt wedding gift (web:1Kgs.9.16), the store-and-chariot cities (web:1Kgs.9.19), the Canaanite remnant conscripted 'to this day' versus the Israelites who serve as soldiers and officers (web:1Kgs.9.20-22, a setumah after 9:22, single-witness, weakly tracking the classification's end), and the count of five hundred fifty chief officers (web:1Kgs.9.23) that answers the officer figures of 5:16.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Continuing through 9:24-25 to keep all the residual Solomon notices in one dossier — rejected because 9:24 opens with the restrictive particle אך and a different topic (the queen's relocation), while the corvée account is internally complete from heading to officer count; the miscellany that follows lacks this document's own framing formula.

boundary_rationale: Two brief closure notices wind up the building program: the restrictive-particle notice אך בת־פרעה עלתה — Pharaoh's daughter moves from David's city to her purpose-built house, triggering the Millo construction ('Then he built Millo', web:1Kgs.9.24, resolving the notices of 3:1 and 7:8) — and the cultic-regularity notice of Solomon's three-times-yearly burnt and peace offerings on the altar, ending ושלם את־הבית, 'So he finished the house' (web:1Kgs.9.25, oshb:1Kgs.9.25). The pair belongs together as the program's punch-list: each verse discharges a thread the temple-palace complex left open, and the שלם completion echo closes the sequence begun at 6:1 for good.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Assigning each notice its own row on their separate topics — rejected because two adjacent single-verse rows would breach the campaign's minimum-unit discipline for material that shares one function (program wind-up) and one register (retrospective annal notice), with no scene or speech in either verse; the topical seam is recorded here instead of being promoted to a boundary.

boundary_rationale: A fronted-object annal opening — ואני עשה המלך שלמה, 'King Solomon made a fleet of ships' (oshb:1Kgs.9.26) — starts a self-contained maritime notice: the Ezion-Geber shipyard located by Eloth on the Red Sea in Edom (web:1Kgs.9.26), Hiram's expert sailors seconded to Solomon's crews (web:1Kgs.9.27), and the Ophir run returning four hundred twenty talents of gold (web:1Kgs.9.28), where the WLC petuchah (single-witness) weakly seconds the notice's end. The Sheba narrative then opens on its own fronted subject and hearing motive at 10:1; the fleet reappears at 10:11 only as a cross-referenced aside.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the fleet notice into ch. 10 to unite all Ophir material — rejected because 10:1 opens a narrative scene with new principals while 9:26-28 is pure annal; the later almug aside explicitly re-identifies 'the fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir', which is quotation of this notice, not continuation of it.

literature_type_guess: state_visit_narrative (the queen of Sheba) with fleet parenthesis
boundary_rationale: A fronted-subject opening with hearing motive — ומלכת שבא שמעת את־שמע שלמה לשם יהוה, 'When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning Yahweh's name' (oshb:1Kgs.10.1) — launches the visit narrative: arrival with the spice caravan, the hard questions all answered (web:1Kgs.10.2-3), the breathless inventory of wisdom, table, and ascent that leaves 'no more spirit in her' (web:1Kgs.10.4-5), her testimony speech climaxing in the blessing of Yahweh who set Solomon on the throne 'to do justice and righteousness' (web:1Kgs.10.6-9), and the exchange of gifts (web:1Kgs.10.10). The narrator's additive parenthesis on Hiram's fleet and the unmatched almug wood (וגם אני חירם, web:1Kgs.10.11-12) interrupts associatively — keyed by the Ophir gold and precious stones just mentioned — and the resumptive fronted clause והמלך שלמה נתן returns to the queen for the counter-gift and departure formula 'she turned and went to her own land' (web:1Kgs.10.13), with a WLC setumah following (single-witness, weak accord). Arrival to departure is the unit's envelope.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Excising the almug parenthesis 10:11-12 as its own annal row — a live option given its register shift — rejected because the aside opens with the additive particle וגם hooking it to 10:10's gift list, carries no independent frame formula (contrast the word-event interrupt at 6:11), and sits inside the visit's gift-exchange envelope whose resumption at 10:13 the campaign treats as parenthesis-closure, following the narrator-aside precedent carried from Samuel.

boundary_rationale: A revenue heading — ויהי משקל הזהב אשר־בא לשלמה בשנה אחת, 'Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents' (oshb:1Kgs.10.14) — opens the treasury annal: merchant and vassal income (web:1Kgs.10.15), the two hundred bucklers and three hundred shields of beaten gold deposited in the House of the Forest of Lebanon (web:1Kgs.10.16-17, a petuchah after 10:17 in the WLC, single-witness, tracking the armory entry only), the ivory throne with its six steps and twelve lions 'nothing like it in any kingdom' (web:1Kgs.10.18-20), the all-gold vessels with silver 'considered of little value' (web:1Kgs.10.21), and the Tarshish fleet's triennial cargo of gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks (web:1Kgs.10.22). The register holds together as one inventory of surplus; the next verse turns from inventory to verdict.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking out the ivory throne 10:18-20 as a craft entry in the ch. 7 manner — a live option, since oshb:1Kgs.10.16 and 10.18 do open with the same ויעש-plus-object frame that opens chapter 7's bronze and gold entries, though there with a different subject — Hiram or Solomon named directly, never המלך — rejected instead because none of these items carries an entry's own completion or closing formula (contrast ותתם at oshb:1Kgs.7.22 and the uniformity colophon at 7.37): the bucklers, shields, and throne are chained by simple parataxis inside one revenue heading rather than closed one at a time, and the incomparability tag on the throne matches the annal's superlative register rather than a craft record's specification style.

boundary_rationale: The verdict formula ויגדל המלך שלמה מכל מלכי הארץ — 'So King Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom' (oshb:1Kgs.10.23) — steps back from inventory to judgment, reprising the two gifts of the Gibeon dream in one sentence. The summary continues with the world's pilgrimage to hear the God-given wisdom (web:1Kgs.10.24, echoing 4:34) and the standing tribute schedule — silver and gold vessels, clothing, armor, spices, horses, mules, 'year after year' (web:1Kgs.10.25). A WLC setumah follows 10:25 (single-witness) in weak agreement with the summary's end before the military-procurement notice opens.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 10:23-25 as the conclusion of the wealth annal 10:14-22 — rejected because the ויגדל formula is evaluative rather than inventorial, and the pilgrimage-plus-tribute pair generalizes over the whole Solomon account (wisdom and wealth together), forming the cycle's summarizing cadence just before the apostasy chapter reverses it.

boundary_rationale: A procurement formula — ויאסף שלמה רכב ופרשים, 'Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen' (oshb:1Kgs.10.26) — opens the cycle's last prosperity notice: the counts (one thousand four hundred chariots, twelve thousand horsemen) and their garrisoning (web:1Kgs.10.26), the silver-as-stones and cedar-as-sycamore hyperboles (web:1Kgs.10.27), and the Egypt horse trade with fixed prices — six hundred shekels a chariot, one hundred fifty a horse — re-exported to the Hittite and Syrian kings (web:1Kgs.10.28-29). The WLC petuchah after 10:29 (single-witness) weakly accords with the chapter's end; 11:1 then opens the apostasy complex on a contrastive fronted subject and the loving of many foreign women.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging the horse trade into the greatness summary — rejected because 10:26 returns from evaluative generalization to concrete procurement annal with fresh figures and a distinct commercial topic; the two registers alternate rather than continue, and the trade notice's Deuteronomic resonance (multiplying horses from Egypt) gives it a function of its own on the threshold of ch. 11's judgment.

boundary_rationale: A contrastive fronted subject reverses the cycle's direction — והמלך שלמה אהב נשים נכריות רבות, 'Now King Solomon loved many foreign women' (oshb:1Kgs.11.1) — and the indictment builds in the narrator's voice: the forbidden nations with the intermarriage citation (web:1Kgs.11.2), the seven hundred and three hundred, the heart turned in old age 'not perfect... as the heart of David his father' (web:1Kgs.11.3-4), Ashtoreth and Milcom, the high places for Chemosh and Molech (web:1Kgs.11.5-8). Divine anger follows with the two-appearances reminder (web:1Kgs.11.9-10), and the judgment speech completes the arc: kingdom torn, deferred for David's sake, one tribe reserved 'for Jerusalem's sake which I have chosen' (web:1Kgs.11.11-13). Indictment, anger, verdict form one prosecutorial sequence; the adversary narratives that execute the sentence then open with their own raising formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Detaching the judgment speech 11:11-13 as an oracle unit — rejected because no word-event or vision formula frames it (contrast 6:11); ויאמר יהוה לשלמה continues the anger clause of 11:9 directly, making the speech the indictment's issue rather than a separately-framed revelation. The WLC setumah after 11:6 and petuchah after 11:10 (both single-witness) articulate indictment stages and receive no boundary force.

boundary_rationale: The raising formula ויקם יהוה שטן לשלמה את הדד האדמי (oshb:1Kgs.11.14) opens the first execution of the ch. 11 sentence: a biographical flashback to Joab's six-month extermination in Edom (web:1Kgs.11.15-16, narrator parentheses), the child Hadad's flight via Midian and Paran to Pharaoh's court (web:1Kgs.11.17-18), the royal marriage to Tahpenes's sister and Genubath's rearing among Pharaoh's sons (web:1Kgs.11.19-20), and the hearing notice — David and Joab dead — that triggers the departure request and the closing exchange with Pharaoh: 'Nothing, however only let me depart' (web:1Kgs.11.21-22). The unit ends on that open-ended dialogue, and the parallel raising formula at 11:23 opens its twin.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Hadad and Rezon into one adversaries panel — rejected because the text builds them as parallel but discrete frames, each launched by its own ויקם... שטן formula with distinct geography (Edom-Egypt vs Zobah-Damascus); the deliberate doubling is the literary device, and collapsing it would erase the very patterning that binds ch. 11's judgment to its execution.

boundary_rationale: The twin raising formula — ויקם אלהים לו שטן את רזון בן־אלידע (oshb:1Kgs.11.23) — opens the compact second adversary notice: the fugitive from Hadadezer of Zobah who gathered a troop, took Damascus, and reigned there (web:1Kgs.11.24), with the summarizing verdict that he opposed Israel 'all the days of Solomon, in addition to the mischief of Hadad', abhorring Israel and reigning over Syria (web:1Kgs.11.25). That כל־ימי שלמה summary is the notice's own closure, cross-tying both adversaries, and the WLC petuchah after 11:25 (single-witness) sits in weak agreement; 11:26 then pivots to an adversary of a different kind with a fronted Israelite name.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the three-verse notice as too slight for a row and folding it into the Hadad narrative — rejected because the raising formula is the panel's structuring device and the notice carries complete narrative anatomy (origin, rise, reign, verdict) in annalistic compression; brevity is a feature of the register, not evidence of dependence.

boundary_rationale: A fronted-subject introduction in the adversary series' cadence — וְיָרָבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט...וַיָּרֶם יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ, Jeroboam of Zeredah, Solomon's own industrious officer over the house of Joseph's corvée, 'lifted up his hand against the king' (oshb:1Kgs.11.26) — opens the climactic third panel, and the narrator's reason clause restates the same charge in its own words, וְזֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר הֵרִים יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ, 'this is the reason he lifted up his hand against the king' (oshb:1Kgs.11.27), ahead of the Millo-and-breach building notice (web:1Kgs.11.27b) and the corvée-appointment notice (web:1Kgs.11.28). Its substance is the road encounter 'at that time': Ahijah the Shilonite, the new garment torn in twelve pieces, ten given to Jeroboam (web:1Kgs.11.29-31), and the oracle unpacking the sign — ten tribes, one tribe for David's lamp in Jerusalem, the conditional sure-house offer to Jeroboam, affliction 'but not forever' (web:1Kgs.11.32-39). Solomon's kill attempt and Jeroboam's flight to Shishak 'until the death of Solomon' (web:1Kgs.11.40) close the panel with the fugitive parked for ch. 12.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 11:29's temporal formula (ויהי בעת ההיא) to give the sign-act oracle its own row — a genuine option — rejected because 11:26's charge that Jeroboam 'lifted up his hand against the king' is narratively cashed out only by the Ahijah designation and the flight it provokes: the introduction has no event of its own, and severing it would leave a three-verse biographical fragment whose announced rebellion never occurs inside it. The WLC setumot after 11:28 and 11:39 (single-witness) mark internal stages under the weak tier.

boundary_rationale: The book's regnal framework debuts its closing member: the source citation ויתר דברי שלמה... הלוא־הם כתבים על־ספר דברי שלמה, 'aren't they written in the book of the acts of Solomon?' (oshb:1Kgs.11.41), the forty-year reign total (web:1Kgs.11.42), and the death-burial-succession chain — slept with his fathers, buried in David's city, 'and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place' (web:1Kgs.11.43). The three-member formula (source, length, succession) closes the entire Solomon cycle; a WLC setumah follows (single-witness) in weak accord, and 12:1 opens at Shechem with a movement formula and a new protagonist.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the regnal close to the Jeroboam panel it follows — rejected because 11:41-43 evaluates the whole reign in the annal register (matching 2:10-12's frame for David), while 11:26-40 is scene narrative about another man; the formula's function is precisely to seal a reign, and this campaign keeps each instance as its own framework row.

boundary_rationale: The movement formula וילך רחבעם שכם — 'Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king' (oshb:1Kgs.12.1) — opens one continuous negotiation drama: the yoke petition with Jeroboam recalled from Egypt (web:1Kgs.12.2-4), the three-day adjournment (12:5), the counsel of the elders and its abandonment for the young men's scorpions speech (web:1Kgs.12.6-11), the harsh answer on the third day (web:1Kgs.12.12-14), the narrator's fulfillment aside — 'a thing brought about from Yahweh, that he might establish his word... by Ahijah' (web:1Kgs.12.15) — the secession cry 'What portion have we in David? To your tents, Israel!' (web:1Kgs.12.16), the Judah remnant notice (12:17, a petuchah after, single-witness, recorded without force), Adoram stoned and the king's flight (web:1Kgs.12.18), and the etiological seal: 'So Israel rebelled against David's house to this day' (web:1Kgs.12.19, setumah after, single-witness, in weak accord). The counsel rounds are turns inside one assembly event held at one location on one announced timetable.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 12:16 between the harsh answer and the secession — rejected because the people's cry is the direct answer-to-the-answer inside the same convened assembly, and the fulfillment aside at 12:15 binds cause to consequence across that very seam; the narrative's own timetable (return on the third day) frames 12:12-19 as the assembly's final session, not a new scene.

boundary_rationale: A hearing formula constitutes the northern kingdom — ויהי כשמע כל־ישראל כי־שב ירבעם, all Israel hears of Jeroboam's return, summons him to the congregation, and crowns him, 'no one who followed David's house, except for the tribe of Judah only' (oshb:1Kgs.12.20) — and the counter-move follows: Rehoboam back in Jerusalem musters a hundred eighty thousand warriors of Judah and Benjamin 'to bring the kingdom again' (web:1Kgs.12.21). The word-event formula ויהי דבר האלהים אל־שמעיה (web:1Kgs.12.22) interdicts the campaign — 'You shall not go up or fight against your brothers... for this thing is from me' — and the compliance notice closes the unit: 'they listened to Yahweh's word, and returned and went their way' (web:1Kgs.12.24, a setumah after, single-witness, weakly seconding the close). Coronation, muster, and halt form the schism's constitutional settlement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 12:20 to the schism narrative as its coda — rejected because 12:19's 'to this day' formula is an etiological close, and this campaign's device matrix bars closes from opening; the hearing formula at 12:20 launches consequence-action (a coronation, then a muster, then an oracle) that plays out after the assembly has dissolved and in different locations.

literature_type_guess: cult_innovation_account (the golden calves of Bethel and Dan)
boundary_rationale: A building formula reopens Jeroboam's file — ויבן ירבעם את־שכם בהר אפרים... ויבן את־פנואל (oshb:1Kgs.12.25) — and the account proceeds from fortification to cult: the interior monologue fearing pilgrimage to Jerusalem ('they will kill me', web:1Kgs.12.26-27), the counsel and the two golden calves with the exodus acclamation 'Look and behold your gods, Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt!' (web:1Kgs.12.28), their stationing at Bethel and Dan (12:29), the narrator's verdict 'This thing became a sin' (web:1Kgs.12.30), the high-place houses and non-Levitical priesthood (12:31), and the self-devised eighth-month feast at the Bethel altar (web:1Kgs.12.32-33). The account closes with Jeroboam ascending the altar to burn incense — the tableau on which ch. 13 breaks in — with a WLC petuchah after 12:33 (single-witness) in weak agreement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the unit into 13:1-10 since the man of God interrupts the very altar ascent 12:33 narrates — rejected because 13:1's והנה presentative introduces a new principal 'out of Judah by Yahweh's word' while restating Jeroboam's altar position as a circumstantial clause: that re-setting is episode-opening machinery, and the confrontation runs on the man of God's commission, a different narrative program from the cult-founding dossier.

boundary_rationale: The presentative opening והנה איש אלהים בא מיהודה בדבר יהוה (oshb:1Kgs.13.1) breaks into the altar tableau of 12:33 with a new principal and a re-set stage (Jeroboam's position restated as a circumstantial clause). The scene arcs from the apostrophized oracle — 'Altar! Altar!... a son will be born to David's house, Josiah by name' (web:1Kgs.13.2) — through the same-day sign (13:3), the withered hand and the altar split 'according to the sign' (web:1Kgs.13.4-5), the intercession and restoration (13:6), and the refused invitation grounded in the threefold command — no bread, no water, no returning by the way — to the compliance exit 'So he went another way' (web:1Kgs.13.8-10). The WLC petuchah after 13:10 (single-witness) weakly accords with the exit's closure; 13:11 then introduces a resident of Bethel with a fronted-subject formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through the old-prophet pursuit since the same commissioned command governs both — rejected because 13:11 opens on new scene machinery (a previously unmentioned character introduced with his own nominal clause, at his own house, informed second-hand by his sons); the shared command is the two episodes' thematic hinge, which the campaign records as a relation rather than a merge.

literature_type_guess: prophetic_conflict_legend (the old prophet and the disobedient man of God)
boundary_rationale: A fronted nominal introduction — ונביא אחד זקן ישב בבית־אל, 'Now an old prophet lived in Bethel' (oshb:1Kgs.13.11) — opens the book's strangest continuous arc: the sons' report, the donkey saddled, the oak-tree interception (web:1Kgs.13.14), the refused invitation re-quoting the command, the angel-lie — 'He lied to him' (web:1Kgs.13.18) — the table oracle mid-meal announcing no burial with the fathers (web:1Kgs.13.20-22, a petuchah after 13:20 in the WLC, single-witness, mid-scene, recorded without force), the lion that kills but neither eats the body nor mauls the donkey (web:1Kgs.13.24, 13.28), the retrieval, the 'Alas, my brother!' mourning and own-grave burial (web:1Kgs.13.29-30), and the bones charge with its confirmation that the Bethel oracle 'will surely happen' — extended to 'the cities of Samaria' (web:1Kgs.13.31-32). The charge's forward look ends the legend; the WLC petuchah after 13:32 (single-witness) agrees weakly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 13:23 where the fatal journey begins — rejected because the lion episode is the table oracle's execution, narrated by the same cast within one continuous itinerary (house, road, house), and the old prophet's own interpretation at 13:26 explicitly binds death to the oracle 'according to Yahweh's word which he spoke to him'; severing sentence from execution would cut the legend at its theological hinge.

boundary_rationale: The retrospective frame אחר הדבר הזה — 'After this thing, Jeroboam didn't turn from his evil way' (oshb:1Kgs.13.33) — steps out of scene narrative into editorial verdict: the reconstituted anyone-who-wants priesthood of the high places (web:1Kgs.13.33) and the sentence formula 'This thing became sin to the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off and to destroy it from off the surface of the earth' (web:1Kgs.13.34), which sharpens 12:30's 'became a sin' into a house-destruction verdict and sets the docket for Ahijah's oracle in ch. 14. The WLC petuchah after 13:34 (single-witness) weakly seconds the coda's end, and 14:1 opens with its own temporal formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the coda to the old-prophet legend as its application — rejected because 13:33-34 returns to Jeroboam, who is absent from 13:11-32 entirely, and the register reverts from legend to the annalistic evaluation stream begun at 12:30; the verses assess the king's response to the whole Bethel complex, functioning as the section's editorial close.

boundary_rationale: The temporal formula בעת ההיא חלה אביה בן־ירבעם (oshb:1Kgs.14.1) opens a consultation narrative built on disguise and unmasking: Jeroboam's commission to his wife with the ten loaves and honey (web:1Kgs.14.2-3), the journey to blind Ahijah forewarned by Yahweh — 'she will pretend to be another woman' (web:1Kgs.14.4-5) — the doorstep exposure 'Come in, Jeroboam's wife! Why do you pretend to be another? For I am sent to you with heavy news' (web:1Kgs.14.6), whose promised freight follows at once: the dynastic judgment oracle reciting exaltation, tearing, and calf-making, sentencing the house to be swept 'as a man sweeps away dung' with the dogs-and-birds burial curse (web:1Kgs.14.7-11), the child's death timed to her feet entering the city with the sole-grave concession (web:1Kgs.14.12-13), the coming king who will cut the house off, and Israel's uprooting beyond the River for the Asherah poles (web:1Kgs.14.14-16). Execution follows immediately: threshold, death, burial, 'according to Yahweh's word... by his servant Ahijah' (web:1Kgs.14.17-18) — the fulfillment notice that closes the unit before the regnal formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between oracle and execution at 14:17 — rejected because the wife's return is the oracle's own stipulated sign ('When your feet enter into the city, the child will die', 14:12) and the fulfillment formula at 14:18 is this book's characteristic unit-closer; oracle and verification form one prophetic transaction, as with 2:26-27 and 13:23-26. The WLC setumot after 14:4 and 14:9 (single-witness) mark internal stages under the weak tier.

boundary_rationale: The framework's closing member for the north's first king: the source citation with its distinctive war note — ויתר דברי ירבעם אשר נלחם ואשר מלך, 'how he fought and how he reigned... written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel' (oshb:1Kgs.14.19) — and the twenty-two-year total with death and Nadab's succession (web:1Kgs.14.20). This is the first occurrence of the chronicles-of-Israel citation that will close every northern reign; the WLC petuchah after 14:20 (single-witness) weakly accords with the formula's end, and 14:21 opens the parallel Judahite frame.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the close into the Ahijah narrative — rejected because the formula is register-switching machinery (annal, not scene) and pointedly ignores the oracle it follows, citing instead the archival record; the campaign keeps each framework member as its own row to preserve the alternation structure that organizes chs. 14-16.

boundary_rationale: The Judahite frame opens on a fronted subject — ורחבעם בן־שלמה מלך ביהודה (oshb:1Kgs.14.21) — with the full accession data set: age forty-one, seventeen years in Jerusalem 'the city which Yahweh had chosen', and the queen-mother notice, Naamah the Ammonitess (web:1Kgs.14.21). The evaluation follows in the negative: Judah did evil above the fathers, high places and pillars and Asherah poles 'on every high hill and under every green tree', and the qedeshim doing 'according to all the abominations of the nations' (web:1Kgs.14.22-24). Opening data plus evaluation form the frame's front member; the WLC petuchah after 14:24 (single-witness) weakly seconds its close before the dated Shishak notice.
