strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the frame through the Shishak invasion as one Rehoboam account — rejected because 14:25 carries its own regnal-year date formula (ויהי בשנה החמישית למלך רחבעם), the marker this book uses to introduce discrete events within a reign; the frame member is durative evaluation, the invasion a dated occurrence.

boundary_rationale: A regnal-year date formula — 'In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem' (web:1Kgs.14.25, oshb:1Kgs.14.25) — opens the reign's one narrated event: the stripping of both treasuries including 'all the gold shields which Solomon had made' (web:1Kgs.14.26, undoing 10:16-17), the bronze replacements committed to the guard captains (web:1Kgs.14.27), and the iterative procedure notice — borne when the king enters Yahweh's house, returned to the guard room (web:1Kgs.14.28) — whose durative cadence closes the notice. The regnal closing formula then begins at 14:29 with its source citation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging the invasion into the closing formula as reign miscellany — rejected because 14:25-28 is a dated event notice with narrative consequence (gold to bronze, the kingdom's diminishment dramatized in hardware), while 14:29-31 is pure framework; the bronze-shields procedure is the annal's own coda, not part of the archival citation.

boundary_rationale: The Judahite closing frame: source citation to 'the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah' (web:1Kgs.14.29, ויתר דברי רחבעם at oshb:1Kgs.14.29), the standing-war notice 'There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually' (web:1Kgs.14.30), and the death-burial-succession chain with the queen-mother notice repeated — Naamah the Ammonitess — and Abijam's accession (web:1Kgs.14.31). The WLC petuchah after 14:31 (single-witness) weakly accords with the frame's end; 15:1 opens the next reign with its synchronism formula ('In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the war notice 14:30 as a separate annal member — rejected because the continual-war formula is a standard element inside the closing frame (recurring at 15:6-7 and 15:16 in equivalent positions), a one-verse row would breach minimum-unit discipline, and the notice shares the frame's summarizing durative register.

boundary_rationale: The synchronism formula opens — ובשנת שמנה עשרה למלך ירבעם, 'in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam... Abijam began to reign over Judah' (oshb:1Kgs.15.1) — and the short reign runs frame to frame: three years, queen mother Maacah (web:1Kgs.15.2), the negative evaluation with the David's-lamp concession and its Uriah-only exception (web:1Kgs.15.3-5), the inherited war notice (15:6), the source citation to the chronicles of Judah with the Abijam-Jeroboam war note (web:1Kgs.15.7), and death-burial-succession to Asa (web:1Kgs.15.8), a WLC petuchah following (single-witness) in weak accord. With no narrated event inside, opening and closing formulas fuse into one framework row.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Peeling the theological aside 15:4-5 into its own row — rejected because the lamp-for-David's-sake comment is the evaluation's own qualification (syntactically dependent on 15:3's negative verdict), matching the qualifying clauses embedded in other frames (compare 15:14), not an independent notice.

boundary_rationale: Asa's frame opens on the synchronism ובשנת עשרים לירבעם (oshb:1Kgs.15.9) with the forty-one-year figure and the queen-mother notice (web:1Kgs.15.10), and the rare positive evaluation 'right in Yahweh's eyes, as David his father' (web:1Kgs.15.11) governs a reform report: qedeshim expelled, ancestral idols removed (15:12), Maacah herself deposed and her Asherah image cut down and burned at the Kidron (web:1Kgs.15.13), the high-places qualification balanced by the perfect heart (web:1Kgs.15.14), and the dedicated silver, gold, and utensils restored to Yahweh's house (web:1Kgs.15.15) — the treasury notice on which the next unit's treasury raid turns. The war formula at 15:16 then opens the reign's event narrative.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the frame through the Baasha war to 15:22 as one Asa account — rejected not because 15:16's durative ומלחמה היתה בין אסא ובין בעשא...כל ימיהם opens event material 'elsewhere' in this framework (it does not: the same formula — with Rehoboam and Jeroboam as antagonists and כל הימים rather than כל ימיהם as its tail — is frame-internal at 14:30 and sits inside the source-citation verse itself at 15:7), but because 15:16 functions here as a summary heading naming the two antagonists of the wayyiqtol narrative that begins at oshb:1Kgs.15.17 (וַיַּעַל בַּעְשָׁא), a heading its own verbatim repetition at 15:32 brackets around that whole narrative in a summary-then-expansion pattern. The reform report remains evaluation-governed and the following material scene-governed, so the frame/event seam still falls at 15:15/15:16.

literature_type_guess: war_and_treaty_narrative (Ramah blockade and the Ben-Hadad purchase)
boundary_rationale: The durative war formula ומלחמה היתה בין אסא ובין בעשא (oshb:1Kgs.15.16) heads the reign's one narrated conflict: Baasha fortifies Ramah to seal Judah's border (web:1Kgs.15.17); Asa empties both treasuries — the very stores 15:15 had just replenished — for Ben-Hadad of Damascus with the treaty speech 'Go, break your treaty with Baasha' (web:1Kgs.15.18-19); Aram strikes Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, Chinneroth, and Naphtali (web:1Kgs.15.20); Baasha abandons Ramah for Tirzah (15:21); and Asa's no-exemption proclamation carries off Ramah's stones and timber to build Geba and Mizpah (web:1Kgs.15.22) — the dismantling notice that closes the episode with the border re-drawn. The closing formula's source citation follows at 15:23.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 15:20 between diplomacy and result — rejected because Ben-Hadad's strike, Baasha's withdrawal, and the Ramah salvage are the treaty's stipulated outcome chain ('that he may depart from me', 15:19) inside one continuous cause-and-effect narrative; no formula or scene reset intervenes.

boundary_rationale: Asa's closing frame: the expanded source citation — 'all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built' — in the chronicles of Judah, with the old-age feet-disease note (web:1Kgs.15.23), then the death-burial-succession chain to Jehoshaphat in David's city (web:1Kgs.15.24), a WLC petuchah after (single-witness) weakly seconding the frame's end. The narrative then crosses to the north with Nadab's accession formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding the disease note apart as biographical annal — rejected because the רק-qualified note sits inside the citation verse itself as the frame's customary qualification (the same slot the war notes occupy at 14:30 and 15:7), and a sub-verse split is unavailable to this campaign's row grammar.

boundary_rationale: The northern file resumes on a fronted subject with synchronism — ונדב בן־ירבעם מלך על־ישראל בשנת שתים לאסא (oshb:1Kgs.15.25) — and Nadab's two-year reign carries its evaluation (walking in his father's way and sin, web:1Kgs.15.26), the Gibbethon conspiracy in which Baasha strikes him during the siege (web:1Kgs.15.27-28), the dynastic annihilation 'He didn't leave to Jeroboam any who breathed' with the fulfillment formula tying it to Ahijah's oracle and grounding it in Jeroboam's sins (web:1Kgs.15.29-30), the source citation (15:31), and the Asa-Baasha war notice (web:1Kgs.15.32) that rounds off the file, a WLC petuchah following (single-witness, weak accord). Reign, coup, and fulfillment form one short dynastic dossier.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the annihilation-fulfillment verses 15:29-30 as an oracle-execution row — rejected because they continue Baasha's accession actions in the same wayyiqtol chain ('As soon as he was king, he struck...'), and the fulfillment formula functions here as it does at 14:18 and 2:27 — closing narrative, not opening it; the row would also orphan the source citation from the reign it archives.

boundary_rationale: Baasha's frame opens with the bare synchronism בשנת שלש לאסא... מלך בעשא (oshb:1Kgs.15.33) and the twenty-four-year Tirzah reign with the Jeroboam-way evaluation (web:1Kgs.15.34, a setumah after in the WLC, single-witness, articulating frame from oracle). The word-event formula ויהי דבר־יהוה אל־יהוא בן־חנני (web:1Kgs.16.1) delivers the dust-to-prince indictment and the Jeroboam-pattern sentence with the dogs-and-birds curse (web:1Kgs.16.2-4), after which the closing frame archives the reign (source citation, death, burial in Tirzah, Elah's succession, web:1Kgs.16.5-6) and the narrator's appendix note re-grounds the oracle 'both because of all the evil... and because he struck him' (web:1Kgs.16.7), a petuchah following (single-witness, weak accord). The reign unit spans the chapter seam — versification metadata carries no weight against the file's own frame-to-frame coherence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving Jehu's oracle its own row on the word-event formula — the campaign's usual practice for marked oracles — rejected here because the oracle is the only content between opening and closing formulas of a reign otherwise without event, and the appendix note at 16:7 shows the editor binding oracle and reign-file together retrospectively; a three-row split (frame / oracle / frame-plus-note) would scatter one dossier across fragments none of which could stand alone.

boundary_rationale: The synchronism בשנת עשרים ושש שנה לאסא opens Elah's two-year file (oshb:1Kgs.16.8), whose single event is the coup: Zimri, captain of half the chariots, strikes the king while he is 'drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza' (web:1Kgs.16.9-10). The throne-day extermination of Baasha's house — no male 'among his relatives or his friends' — follows with the fulfillment formula citing Jehu's word and indicting the vanities of father and son (web:1Kgs.16.11-13), and the source citation closes the file (web:1Kgs.16.14), a WLC petuchah after (single-witness) in weak agreement. The next synchronism opens Zimri's seven days.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Elah's file with Zimri's since the same conspirator spans both — rejected because 16:15 opens a new synchronism frame (Zimri's own reign-count begins) and relocates the action to the Gibbethon camp with a new cast; the framework's alternation grammar, not participant continuity, governs file boundaries in these chapters.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_reign_unit (Zimri's seven days and the Tirzah siege)
boundary_rationale: The synchronism formula gives the book's shortest reign — 'Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah' (web:1Kgs.16.15, oshb:1Kgs.16.15) — with the camp at Gibbethon as circumstantial backdrop: the army hears of the conspiracy, crowns Omri in the camp 'that day' (web:1Kgs.16.16), the siege moves to Tirzah (16:17), and Zimri burns the king's house over himself (web:1Kgs.16.18) with the evaluative ground 'for his sins... in walking in the way of Jeroboam' (16:19); the source citation with its treason note closes the file (web:1Kgs.16.20), a WLC petuchah following (single-witness, weak accord). The אז formula at 16:21 then opens the interregnum.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through the Tibni-Omri division since the succession crisis flows from Zimri's death — rejected because 16:20's source citation is the framework's file-closer, and 16:21 opens with the marked archaic אז יחלק construction (the 3:16/8:1 opener class) introducing a two-party struggle in which Zimri plays no part.

boundary_rationale: The archaic opener אז יחלק העם ישראל לחצי — 'Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts' (oshb:1Kgs.16.21) — marks a constitutional anomaly the framework cannot file under any reign: half for Tibni son of Ginath, half for Omri (web:1Kgs.16.21), resolved by the prevailing of Omri's half, Tibni's death, and the laconic וימלך עמרי, 'and Omri reigned' (web:1Kgs.16.22). The WLC petuchah after 16:22 (single-witness) accords weakly with the notice's end, where Omri's own synchronism frame opens at 16:23 — the framework device that dates his sole reign.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Prefixing the division to Omri's reign unit as his rise narrative — rejected because 16:23's synchronism ('In the thirty-first year of Asa') restarts the file grammar for the sole reign exactly as this framework does elsewhere, and because the notice sits in a genuine gap between framework files: 16:20's source citation closes Zimri's dossier and 16:23's synchronism opens Omri's, leaving 16:21-22 claimed by neither. The אז-plus-prefix-form construction opening 16:21 is frequent at narrative onsets (3:16, 8:1) but not reserved for them — oshb:1Kgs.11.7 uses the identical construction mid-indictment inside the apostasy span 11:1-13 — so it corroborates rather than carries the boundary, which rests on the framework gap alone.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_reign_unit (Omri and the founding of Samaria)
boundary_rationale: Omri's sole-reign synchronism — בשנת שלשים ואחת שנה לאסא (oshb:1Kgs.16.23) — opens the file with the twelve-year total split across capitals, and its one event is city-founding: the hill of Samaria bought from Shemer for two talents, built, and named for its former owner (web:1Kgs.16.24). The superlative negative evaluation — 'dealt wickedly above all who were before him', walking in all Jeroboam's way (web:1Kgs.16.25-26) — precedes the source citation with the might note (16:27) and the death-burial-succession chain to Ahab in the new capital (web:1Kgs.16.28), a WLC petuchah after (single-witness, weak accord).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the Samaria purchase as a foundation etiology row — rejected because the notice sits between synchronism and evaluation inside the file's standard slot for reign events (as the Ramah affair sits inside Asa's file), and its naming formula lacks the עד היום הזה etiological seal that would mark an independent tradition unit.

literature_type_guess: regnal_opening_with_escalation_report (Ahab of Israel and the Jericho notice)
boundary_rationale: Ahab's frame opens on the fronted subject with synchronism — ואחאב בן־עמרי מלך על־ישראל בשנת שלשים ושמנה (oshb:1Kgs.16.29) — and the evaluation escalates in stages: evil 'above all that were before him' (web:1Kgs.16.30), the sins of Jeroboam counted 'a light thing' beside the Jezebel marriage and Baal service (web:1Kgs.16.31), the Baal altar and house in Samaria (16:32), the Asherah, and the summary provocation superlative (web:1Kgs.16.33). The era-notice appendix — Hiel of Bethel rebuilding Jericho at the cost of firstborn and youngest 'according to Yahweh's word... by Joshua the son of Nun' (web:1Kgs.16.34) — closes the unit with a fulfillment formula reaching back to Joshua's curse, a setumah following in the WLC (single-witness, weak accord). The Elijah cycle then bursts in at 17:1 with an unintroduced speech formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Making the Hiel notice its own annal row — rejected because בימיו 'in his days' pins the notice inside Ahab's frame as its era-characterizing appendix (the fulfillment-under-apostasy motif completing the evaluation's portrait), and a one-verse row would breach the campaign's minimum-unit discipline for a note the frame itself hosts.

boundary_rationale: Elijah erupts unintroduced — ויאמר אליהו התשבי מתשבי גלעד אל־אחאב, the Tishbite swearing the drought oath 'As Yahweh, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word' (oshb:1Kgs.17.1) — and the word-event command that follows presupposes that confrontation's ground: 'Go away from here (מזה), turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith' (web:1Kgs.17.2-3). The concealment sequence executes it: ravens commanded, bread and meat morning and evening, drinking from the brook (web:1Kgs.17.4-6), until the drying notice — 'the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land' (web:1Kgs.17.7) — closes the episode by the oath's own logic and forces the next move. The WLC sets setumot after both 17:1 and 17:7 (single-witness); the first articulates the oath and is recorded without force under the weak tier, the second weakly seconds the close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving the oath verse its own row as the cycle's superscription, with the word-event formula opening a separate Cherith unit — a serious option the setumah after 17:1 weakly echoes — rejected because a one-verse row breaches the campaign's minimum-unit discipline and the command's deictic 'from here' is anaphoric to the audience with Ahab in 17:1: oath and flight are one narrative motion, cause and immediate consequence.

literature_type_guess: provision_miracle_narrative (the Zarephath widow's meal and oil)
boundary_rationale: The itinerary's second word-event — ויהי דבר־יהוה אליו לאמר, 'Arise, go to Zarephath... I have commanded a widow there to sustain you' (web:1Kgs.17.8-9, the formula at oshb:1Kgs.17.8 repeating 17:2 verbatim as the cycle's movement device) — opens the Sidonian episode: the gate encounter over water and bread (web:1Kgs.17.10-11), the widow's live-Yahweh oath of destitution — a handful of meal, a little oil, two sticks, 'that we may eat it, and die' (web:1Kgs.17.12) — the fear-not commission with the jar oracle 'The jar of meal will not run out... until the day that Yahweh sends rain' (web:1Kgs.17.13-14), and the compliance-plus-duration notice sealed by the fulfillment formula 'according to Yahweh's word, which he spoke by Elijah' (web:1Kgs.17.15-16). The WLC petuchah after 17:16 (single-witness) weakly accords with the fulfillment close; the setumah after 17:13 (single-witness) merely articulates the speech.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending to 17:24 to keep the whole widow-household complex together — rejected because 17:17 opens with the classic new-episode frame ויהי אחר הדברים האלה ('After these things') and a reversal of situation (provision to death), while 17:16's fulfillment formula has already closed the meal-and-oil transaction in the book's standard cadence.

boundary_rationale: The episode frame ויהי אחר הדברים האלה (oshb:1Kgs.17.17) turns provision into crisis: the boy's breathless sickness, the widow's accusation 'You have come to me to bring my sin to memory, and to kill my son!' (web:1Kgs.17.18), the upper-room transfer, Elijah's protest prayer (web:1Kgs.17.19-20), the threefold self-stretching with the soul-return petition (web:1Kgs.17.21), Yahweh's hearing and the revival (17:22), the descent and delivery — 'Behold, your son lives' (web:1Kgs.17.23) — and the widow's recognition formula that crowns both Zarephath episodes: 'Now I know that you are a man of God, and that Yahweh's word in your mouth is truth' (web:1Kgs.17.24). The confession is the unit's and the chapter's close, a WLC petuchah following (single-witness, weak accord) before ch. 18's dated word-event.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between prayer and revival at 17:22 — rejected because petition, hearing, and restoration form one miracle transaction inside one location and cast; the campaign's turn-marker principle covers prayer-and-answer sequences exactly as dialogue turns.

boundary_rationale: A dated word-event reopens the drought plot — ויהי ימים רבים ודבר־יהוה היה אל־אליהו בשנה השלישית, 'Go, show yourself to Ahab; and I will send rain' (web:1Kgs.18.1, oshb:1Kgs.18.1) — and the showing is engineered through an intermediary: the famine notice (18:2), Obadiah's introduction with the narrator's parenthesis on the hundred prophets hidden fifty to a cave (web:1Kgs.18.3-4), the grass-survey commission and the divided routes (web:1Kgs.18.5-6), the road recognition 'Is it you, my lord Elijah?' (web:1Kgs.18.7), and Obadiah's long protest — the kingdom-by-kingdom manhunt, the Spirit-carrying fear, the cave story retold — against the deadly errand (web:1Kgs.18.9-14), answered by Elijah's live-Yahweh oath 'I will surely show myself to him today' (web:1Kgs.18.15). The double movement notice — Obadiah to Ahab, Ahab to Elijah (web:1Kgs.18.16) — discharges the commission and stages the confrontation that opens at 18:17 with its seeing formula. The WLC setumah after 18:14 (single-witness) articulates the protest's end, without force.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing at 18:6 and treating the road encounter as a new scene — rejected because the encounter happens on the very survey routes just divided (the narrative needs Obadiah alone on the way), and the unit's plot question — how Elijah gets before Ahab — remains open until 18:16 hands the meeting over; the episode is one commission-to-delivery arc.

literature_type_guess: confrontation_exchange (troubler of Israel and the Carmel summons)
boundary_rationale: The seeing formula ויהי כראות אחאב את־אליהו (oshb:1Kgs.18.17) finally brings king and prophet face to face for a compact exchange: Ahab's 'Is that you, you troubler of Israel?' (web:1Kgs.18.17), Elijah's counter-indictment — the troubling belongs to the house that forsook the commandments for the Baals (web:1Kgs.18.18) — and the summons that programs the next scene: all Israel to Mount Carmel with the four hundred fifty prophets of Baal and four hundred of the Asherah 'who eat at Jezebel's table' (web:1Kgs.18.19). The exchange ends with that directive; 18:20 narrates its execution with a dispatch formula and a change of location and cast.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the exchange into the Carmel contest as its preamble — rejected because the confrontation is a two-party audience at the meeting point 18:16 arranged, while 18:20 moves to Carmel and assembles all Israel and the prophet corps: location, participants, and speech-register (private accusation versus public trial) all change at the dispatch verse.

boundary_rationale: The dispatch-and-assembly notice — Ahab gathers the prophets to Mount Carmel (web:1Kgs.18.20, וישלח אחאב at oshb:1Kgs.18.20) — opens the great ordeal, one dramatic arc under a single question put in Elijah's wavering challenge: 'If Yahweh is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him', met by silence (web:1Kgs.18.21). The arc proceeds by ordeal procedure — the two-bulls proposal accepted by the people ('The God who answers by fire, let him be God', web:1Kgs.18.22-24), Baal's round from morning to noon with leaping, Elijah's taunt, the self-laceration to no voice (web:1Kgs.18.25-29), the twelve-stone altar repair with the Jacob-naming citation, the trench, and the threefold drenching (web:1Kgs.18.30-35), the evening-offering prayer 'that this people may know that you, Yahweh, are God' (web:1Kgs.18.36-37), the fire that licks up even the water (18:38), the people's prostrate double cry 'Yahweh, he is God!' (web:1Kgs.18.39), and the Kishon slaughter of the prophets (web:1Kgs.18.40) — verdict executed, ordeal complete. The WLC's only mark in the chapter falls earlier, a SAMEKH at 18:14 (single-witness); nothing in the source stands between 18:20 and 18:40, and no weight is drawn from that gap in either direction. The span's boundary rests on the tier-1 case already stated: one question posed at 18:21, one assembly, one day, and the terms of 18:23-24 governing both the Baal round and the altar-repair round alike.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 18:30 where Elijah turns from Baal's failed round to the altar repair — rejected because the two rounds are the ordeal's own paired structure (the terms of 18:23-24 govern both), staged before the same assembled people on the same mountain in one day; halving the contest would sever challenge from verdict.

literature_type_guess: rain_return_narrative (the sevenfold watch and the run to Jezreel)
boundary_rationale: Elijah's word to Ahab pivots the day from fire to water — 'Get up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of abundance of rain' (web:1Kgs.18.41, ויאמר אליהו לאחאב at oshb:1Kgs.18.41) — and the closing movement unfolds: the prophet's crouch on Carmel's summit, face between knees (web:1Kgs.18.42), the servant's sevenfold sea-watch until the hand-sized cloud rises (web:1Kgs.18.43-44), the blackening sky and the great rain that ends the oath of 17:1, Ahab's ride to Jezreel (web:1Kgs.18.45), and the hand-of-Yahweh notice as Elijah tucks his cloak and outruns the chariot to the Jezreel entrance (web:1Kgs.18.46). The arrival at Jezreel closes the unit and the chapter; 19:1 opens inside the city with a telling formula and a new principal, Jezebel.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the rain sequence as the Carmel contest's denouement inside one unit — rejected because 18:41 opens a new transaction with its own progression (announcement, vigil, sign, storm, journey), the assembled people and the ordeal apparatus vanish from view, and the rain resolves the drought frame of 17:1 rather than the fire question of 18:24 — two distinct plot threads receiving two distinct closures.

boundary_rationale: The telling formula ויגד אחאב לאיזבל (oshb:1Kgs.19.1) relays Carmel to Jezebel, whose messenger-oath — 'So let the gods do to me... if I don't make your life as the life of one of them by tomorrow' (web:1Kgs.19.2) — reverses the triumph into flight: Beersheba, the servant left, the day's journey to the juniper, and the death wish 'I am not better than my fathers' (web:1Kgs.19.3-4). The double angelic feeding answers it — the coal-baked cake and water jar, the second touch 'because the journey is too great for you' (web:1Kgs.19.5-7) — and the strength-of-that-food notice carries him forty days and forty nights to 'Horeb, God's Mountain' (web:1Kgs.19.8), where arrival ends the itinerary and the cave scene begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running through the cave dialogue since 19:9 continues the journey's goal — rejected because 19:9's arrival at the cave is immediately marked by והנה דבר־יהוה אליו with the direct question 'What are you doing here, Elijah?': the word-event formula plus locale (the cave, the mountain) opens the theophany audience, a different genre from the flight-provision itinerary that delivers him there.

boundary_rationale: Arrival machinery opens the audience — the cave, the lodging, and והנה דבר־יהוה אליו with the probing 'What are you doing here, Elijah?' (web:1Kgs.19.9, oshb:1Kgs.19.9). The scene is built on exact repetition: the jealous-for-Yahweh answer given twice verbatim (web:1Kgs.19.10, web:1Kgs.19.14, a WLC setumah after 19:14, single-witness, articulating the repetition without force), around the theophany core — wind, earthquake, fire, each negated ('Yahweh was not in...'), then the still small voice and the mantle-wrapped emergence (web:1Kgs.19.11-13). The commission resolves the audience: return by way of Damascus, anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha, the three-sword judgment chain, and the seven-thousand remnant who have not bowed to Baal (web:1Kgs.19.15-18). The commission's close ends the unit; 19:19 departs the mountain with a movement formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the commission 19:15-18 from the theophany — rejected because ויאמר יהוה אליו at 19:15 is the same audience's continuing speech (no scene reset, no new frame), answering the prophet's twice-spoken complaint with marching orders; the question-answer-commission sequence is the theophany's own tripartite anatomy.

boundary_rationale: The departure formula וילך משם — 'So he departed from there' (oshb:1Kgs.19.19) — executes the commission's third clause immediately: Elisha found plowing with twelve yoke, the mantle thrown over him (web:1Kgs.19.19), the run after Elijah with the kiss-my-parents request and the enigmatic 'Go back again; for what have I done to you?' (web:1Kgs.19.20), and the call sealed by burned bridges — oxen slaughtered, boiled with their own equipment, fed to the people — before Elisha 'went after Elijah, and served him' (web:1Kgs.19.21). The service notice closes the call and the chapter, a WLC petuchah following (single-witness, weak accord); ch. 20 opens a different theater entirely with Ben-Hadad's muster.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the call inside the Horeb unit as the commission's execution — rejected because the departure formula moves the scene from the mountain audience to Abel-Meholah's fields with a new second party, and only one of the three anointings is executed here: the call scene is the commission's first installment, not its completion, and stands as its own narrative.

boundary_rationale: A muster-and-siege opening — ובן־הדד מלך־ארם קבץ את־כל־חילו, Ben-Hadad with thirty-two kings besieging Samaria (oshb:1Kgs.20.1) — frames one escalating messenger negotiation: the first demand ('Your silver and your gold are mine...') and Ahab's total capitulation (web:1Kgs.20.2-4), the second demand adding tomorrow's house-search (web:1Kgs.20.5-6), the elders' council — 'Don't listen, and don't consent' (web:1Kgs.20.7-8) — the calibrated refusal (20:9), Ben-Hadad's dust-of-Samaria oath (web:1Kgs.20.10), Israel's armor proverb 'Don't let him who puts on his armor brag like he who takes it off' (web:1Kgs.20.11), and the drunken attack order that ends diplomacy (web:1Kgs.20.12). The exchange arc runs demand to declaration of war; the prophet's sudden approach at 20:13 opens the battle movement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 20:7 where Ahab turns from the enemy's messengers to his own elders — rejected because the council is a deliberative beat inside one continuous negotiation (the same siege, the same demand chain, the answer of 20:9 addressed back to the same messengers); messenger relays are this scene's medium, not its boundaries.

boundary_rationale: The presentative approach formula והנה נביא אחד נגש אל־אחאב (web:1Kgs.20.13) injects the prophetic word into the siege: the delivery oracle with its recognition aim — 'Then you will know that I am Yahweh' — the tactical exchange 'By whom?... Who shall begin?' (web:1Kgs.20.14), the tiny muster of two hundred thirty-two province-princes' young men before seven thousand (web:1Kgs.20.15), the noon sortie against a drunk command tent and the take-them-alive order (web:1Kgs.20.16-18), the man-for-man strike and Syrian rout with Ben-Hadad escaping on horseback (web:1Kgs.20.19-20), and the king's follow-up great slaughter (web:1Kgs.20.21) that closes the engagement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the prophet's return-of-the-year warning 20:22 to the victory account — rejected because 20:22 opens with a fresh approach formula (ויגש הנביא) and its speech is not battle narrative but planning counsel for the next campaign season, pairing structurally with the enemy's own counsel scene at 20:23-25; the two war councils form the interlude between the year's two campaigns.

boundary_rationale: Two advisory scenes bracket the campaign year: the prophet's fresh approach — ויגש הנביא אל־מלך ישראל, 'strengthen yourself... for at the return of the year, the king of Syria will come up against you' (web:1Kgs.20.22, a WLC setumah following, single-witness, articulating the pair's first member) — and the Syrian servants' theological strategy session: 'Their god is a god of the hills... let's fight against them in the plain', with the kings-for-captains reorganization and the horse-for-horse re-muster, accepted by Ben-Hadad (web:1Kgs.20.23-25). The WLC petuchah after 20:25 (single-witness) weakly seconds the interlude's close, where the return-of-the-year formula at 20:26 opens the Aphek campaign both councils anticipated.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Assigning each council to the battle it borders (20:22 backward, 20:23-25 forward) — rejected because the two scenes mirror each other as deliberate composition (each side reading the last battle, each planning the next), and the oracle of 20:28 answers the hills-god theory of 20:23 across the unit seam not verbatim but by quotation-with-substitution: it repeats the epithet אֱלֹהֵי הָרִים and then swaps in יְהוָה for the Syrians' אֱלֹהֵיהֶם and עֲמָקִים for their בַּמִּישׁוֹר, converting a tactical claim into a theological one — a correspondence the campaign records as a relation while keeping the symmetrical council pair intact.

boundary_rationale: The awaited formula arrives — ויהי לתשובת השנה, 'At the return of the year, Ben Hadad mustered the Syrians and went up to Aphek' (web:1Kgs.20.26) — and the campaign unfolds: Israel 'like two little flocks of young goats' against a country-filling host (web:1Kgs.20.27), the man of God's oracle answering the hills-god slander — 'therefore I will deliver all this great multitude into your hand' (web:1Kgs.20.28) — the seven-day standoff, the hundred-thousand-in-a-day battle, and the wall of Aphek falling on twenty-seven thousand (web:1Kgs.20.29-30, a WLC setumah after 20:30, single-witness, at the flight into the inner room, without force), then the sackcloth-and-ropes embassy trading on Israel's merciful kings, the loaded 'He is my brother', the omen-seizing courtiers, and the chariot elevation (web:1Kgs.20.31-33), closing with Ben-Hadad's restitution terms and Ahab's covenant release — וישלחהו, 'So he made a covenant with him and let him go' (web:1Kgs.20.34, setumah after, single-witness, in weak accord). The release is the hinge the judgment scene will condemn.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between battle and surrender negotiation at 20:31 — rejected because the embassy issues directly from the flight of 20:30 within one continuous aftermath (same day-sequence, same fugitive king), and the campaign's plot completes only at the release: victory, mercy, and covenant form the single transaction on which the following parable-judgment turns.

boundary_rationale: A new cast and genre open — ואיש אחד מבני הנביאים אמר אל־רעהו בדבר יהוה, 'A certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his fellow by Yahweh's word, Please strike me!' (web:1Kgs.20.35) — with the refusal punished by lion (a compressed re-run of ch. 13's obedience logic, web:1Kgs.20.36) and the second man's compliant blow (20:37). The wounded prophet, disguised by his headband, waylays the king with the guard-parable — the escaped captive, life for life or a talent — and springs the self-sentence: 'So shall your judgment be. You yourself have decided it' (web:1Kgs.20.38-40). The unmasking, the recognition 'one of the prophets', and the oracle — 'your life will take the place of his life, and your people take the place of his people' for releasing the man devoted to destruction (web:1Kgs.20.41-42) — close on Ahab's sullen-and-angry ride home to Samaria (web:1Kgs.20.43), a WLC petuchah following (single-witness, weak accord).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Beginning the unit at 20:38 where the king enters — rejected because the strike-me prelude manufactures the disguise the parable requires (the wound is the costume), and 20:35's בדבר יהוה frame governs the whole sequence; prelude, parable, and verdict are one juridical performance in the Nathan mold.

boundary_rationale: The episode frame ויהי אחר הדברים האלה introduces the property and its principals — Naboth's vineyard beside Ahab's Jezreel palace (web:1Kgs.21.1) — and the crime unfolds in one arc: the purchase offer and the inheritance refusal 'May Yahweh forbid me' (web:1Kgs.21.2-3), the king's sullen-and-angry bed sulk echoing 20:43 (web:1Kgs.21.4), Jezebel's interrogation and takeover — 'Do you now govern the kingdom of Israel?' (web:1Kgs.21.5-7) — the sealed letters scripting fast, perjurers, and stoning (web:1Kgs.21.8-10), the elders' exact compliance and Naboth's death (web:1Kgs.21.11-14), and the possession sequence: Jezebel's 'Arise, take possession' and Ahab's descent to the vineyard (web:1Kgs.21.15-16), where a WLC setumah (single-witness) weakly seconds the arc's close as the word-event formula breaks in on Elijah.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 21:8 where Jezebel's plot machinery begins — rejected because her letter-writing executes the promise just spoken in 21:7 ('I will give you the vineyard') within the same conversation's momentum, and the crime narrative's anatomy — refusal, resentment, conspiracy, murder, possession — is one legal-narrative chain that the judgment oracle then reads as a single act: 'Have you killed and also taken possession?'

literature_type_guess: prophetic_judgment_oracle (dogs in the place of Naboth's blood)
boundary_rationale: The word-event formula ויהי דבר־יהוה אל־אליהו התשבי (web:1Kgs.21.17) commissions the confrontation in the stolen vineyard itself — 'Behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth' — with the double oracle: the crime question 'Have you killed and also taken possession?' and the measure-for-measure sentence 'In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs will lick your blood, even yours' (web:1Kgs.21.18-19). The encounter ignites on recognition — 'Have you found me, my enemy?' (web:1Kgs.21.20) — and the sentence expands to the full dynastic formula: house swept away like Jeroboam's and Baasha's (web:1Kgs.21.21-22), the Jezebel oracle by the rampart of Jezreel (web:1Kgs.21.23), and the dogs-and-birds distich (web:1Kgs.21.24) that closes the oracle series.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the oracle into the narrator's no-one-like-Ahab verdict at 21:25 — rejected because 21:25-26 abandons the second-person oracle frame for retrospective editorial prose marked by the restrictive רק, an evaluation of the whole reign rather than a continuation of the vineyard sentence; the campaign's precedent (13:33-34) keeps such asides as their own coda rows.

boundary_rationale: A restrictive-particle aside interrupts between oracle and repentance — רק לא־היה כאחאב, 'But there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do that which was evil in Yahweh's sight, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up' (web:1Kgs.21.25) — extending the indictment to Amorite-grade idolatry (web:1Kgs.21.26). The two verses are narrator evaluation in the superlative register of 16:30-33, sealing the sold-yourself charge of 21:20 as an era verdict; a WLC setumah follows (single-witness) in weak accord with the aside's end, and 21:27 returns to scene narrative with Ahab's hearing response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the aside as the oracle unit's closing gloss — rejected because the verses speak about Ahab in the third person outside the oracle's quotation frame and generalize over the reign ('according to all that the Amorites did'), matching the free-standing evaluative codas at 12:30 and 13:33-34 rather than the sentence speech they follow.

boundary_rationale: The hearing formula ויהי כשמע אחאב את־הדברים האלה opens the reversal: torn clothes, sackcloth on flesh, fasting, lying in sackcloth, walking softly (web:1Kgs.21.27, a WLC setumah after, single-witness, articulating act from answer), and a second word-event to Elijah reads the act — 'See how Ahab humbles himself before me?' — deferring the evil from his days to his son's (web:1Kgs.21.28-29). The deferral oracle closes the Naboth complex and calibrates the fulfillment clock that 22:38 and the house's fall in 2Kgs will strike; ch. 22 then opens with the three-year peace notice in a new theater.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the repentance into the judgment-oracle unit as its response — rejected because 21:27 opens with its own hearing formula after the narrator's aside has already sealed the oracle scene, and the second word-event formula at 21:28 marks a distinct revelatory moment (judgment revised), giving the three verses the complete anatomy of act, word, and adjusted sentence.

boundary_rationale: A durative peace notice resets the theater — וישבו שלש שנים אין מלחמה בין ארם ובין ישראל (web:1Kgs.22.1, oshb:1Kgs.22.1, a WLC petuchah following the verse, single-witness, articulating the notice under the weak tier) — and the third-year visit formula brings Jehoshaphat down to the king of Israel (web:1Kgs.22.2). The prologue poses the campaign question — 'You know that Ramoth Gilead is ours, and we do nothing?' (web:1Kgs.22.3) — and secures the alliance in Jehoshaphat's formula of total identification: 'I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses' (web:1Kgs.22.4). The commitment made, 22:5's inquiry request pivots the narrative from politics to prophecy.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Beginning the Micaiah unit at 22:1 so that peace notice, visit, and inquiry form one build-up — rejected because 22:5 opens the inquiry drama with its own speech formula and a new agenda (דרש־נא... את־דבר יהוה) that governs everything through 22:28; the political prologue and the prophetic audience are distinct movements, the first supplying the war aim the second contests.

boundary_rationale: Jehoshaphat's request — דרש־נא כיום את־דבר יהוה (oshb:1Kgs.22.5) — convenes the book's great inquiry scene, one audience sustained from the four hundred prophets' unanimous 'Go up' (web:1Kgs.22.6) through Jehoshaphat's probe for a prophet of Yahweh and Ahab's 'I hate him' (web:1Kgs.22.7-8), the summons (22:9), the threshing-floor tableau of two enthroned kings with Zedekiah's iron horns (web:1Kgs.22.10-12), the messenger's coaching answered by Micaiah's live-Yahweh oath (web:1Kgs.22.13-14), the ironic first answer and the king's adjuration (web:1Kgs.22.15-16), the shepherdless-sheep vision (web:1Kgs.22.17), the heavenly-council vision — Yahweh enthroned, the volunteering spirit, 'I will go out and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets' (web:1Kgs.22.19-23) — Zedekiah's cheek-blow and Micaiah's inner-room retort (web:1Kgs.22.24-25), the bread-and-water-of-affliction prison order (web:1Kgs.22.26-27), and the departing test-word: 'If you return at all in peace, Yahweh has not spoken by me. Listen, all you people!' (web:1Kgs.22.28). Every exchange is a turn within the one convened audience; the marching-out notice at 22:29 dissolves it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 22:19 where Micaiah moves from the sheep vision to the council vision — rejected because לכן שמע דבר־יהוה continues the same speech to the same royal bench without any scene machinery: the two visions are the audience's escalating disclosure, and cutting between them would sever the lying-spirit explanation from the false-prophecy scene it explains.

boundary_rationale: The march formula ויעל מלך־ישראל ויהושפט מלך־יהודה רמת גלעד (oshb:1Kgs.22.29) opens the campaign the audience debated: the disguise stratagem against Jehoshaphat's robes (web:1Kgs.22.30), the Syrian king's fight-only-the-king order (web:1Kgs.22.31), the mistaken pursuit of the crying Jehoshaphat (web:1Kgs.22.32-33), the bow drawn 'at random' finding the joints of the armor (web:1Kgs.22.34), the propped king bleeding into the chariot floor until evening death (web:1Kgs.22.35), the sunset cry 'Every man to his city' (web:1Kgs.22.36) — the shepherdless-sheep vision come true — and the burial plus the washing at the pool of Samaria where 'the dogs licked up his blood... according to Yahweh's word which he spoke' (web:1Kgs.22.37-38). The fulfillment formula is the terminal close; the regnal frame follows at 22:39.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the fulfillment notice 22:37-38 from the battle — rejected because the death, transport, burial, and dog-licking chain is one uninterrupted wayyiqtol sequence whose last clause carries כדבר יהוה, a phrase this book uses nine times (12:24, 13:26, 14:18, 15:29, 16:12, 16:34, 17:5, 17:16, 22:38) and places at a genuine unit-final position at 14:18, 16:34, 17:16, and here at 22:38; clause-medial at 17:5; and mid-row at 13:26, 15:29, and 16:12 within this campaign's own chunking (12:24 is not itemized here): the notice consummates the narrative it ends, discharging both 21:19 and 20:42 independently of how the formula behaves at those other verses.

boundary_rationale: Ahab's file closes in the framework register: the source citation with its ivory-house and cities note — ויתר דברי אחאב... ובית השן אשר בנה (oshb:1Kgs.22.39) — and the sleeping-with-the-fathers notice with Ahaziah's succession (web:1Kgs.22.40), a WLC petuchah following (single-witness) in weak accord. The formula archives the reign the preceding narrative just ended; Jehoshaphat's long-deferred opening frame then begins at 22:41.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the close to the death narrative — rejected because 22:37-38 is scene consequence under a fulfillment formula while 22:39-40 is archival evaluation addressed to the reader; the framework's file grammar (the same pairing as 14:18 versus 14:19-20) keeps narrative closure and annalistic closure as separate members.

boundary_rationale: The Judahite frame opens on the fronted subject with synchronism — ויהושפט בן־אסא מלך על־יהודה בשנת ארבע לאחאב (web:1Kgs.22.41 = oshb:1Kgs.22.41, MT numbering identical through 22:42): age thirty-five, twenty-five years, queen mother Azubah (web:1Kgs.22.42), and the positive evaluation in Asa's way with the high-places qualification (web:1Kgs.22.43 — the verse the MT divides in two, its high-places clause counted as MT 22:44, so this row's Hebrew cites run web:1Kgs.22.43 = oshb:1Kgs.22.43+22.44). The peace notice — 'Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel' (web:1Kgs.22.44 = oshb:1Kgs.22.45 MT) — completes the frame's opening member, closing the war era the schism opened; the source citation then begins the closing member. From here to the book's end every original-language citation is dual-mapped (+1 within MT ch. 22).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through the miscellany 22:45-49 as one Jehoshaphat account — rejected because the source-citation formula at WEB 22:45 (= MT 22:46) is the framework's closing-member opener, and the notices that follow it (qedeshim, Edom deputy, wrecked ships) sit inside the closing frame as its customary annal appendix, a slot distinct from the accession-and-evaluation member.

boundary_rationale: The closing member opens with the source citation — 'the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he showed, and how he fought' (web:1Kgs.22.45 = oshb:1Kgs.22.46 MT) — and carries its annal appendix: the qedeshim remnant purge completing Asa's reform (web:1Kgs.22.46 = MT 22:47), the no-king-in-Edom deputy notice (web:1Kgs.22.47 = MT 22:48), the Tarshish ships wrecked at Ezion-Geber before reaching Ophir's gold (web:1Kgs.22.48 = MT 22:49, undoing 9:26-28 in one verse), and the refused joint venture with Ahaziah (web:1Kgs.22.49 = MT 22:50), before the death-burial-succession chain to Jehoram (web:1Kgs.22.50 = oshb:1Kgs.22.51 MT, a WLC setumah following, single-witness, weakly seconding the file's end). All Hebrew citations dual-mapped (+1).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carving the three annal notices 22:47-49 into their own miscellany row — rejected because the framework regularly hosts such notices inside the closing member (Asa's feet at 15:23, Zimri's treason at 16:20), and the notices here are threaded to the citation's own themes ('his might... how he fought'); the frame's death-succession clause at 22:50 closes over them as one file.

literature_type_guess: regnal_opening_formula_with_evaluation (Ahaziah of Israel; reign continues into 2Kgs)
boundary_rationale: The book's last file opens and does not close: Ahaziah's synchronism — אחזיהו בן־אחאב מלך על־ישראל בשמרון בשנת שבע עשרה ליהושפט, two years over Israel (web:1Kgs.22.51 = oshb:1Kgs.22.52 MT) — with the triple-pedigree evaluation 'in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam' (web:1Kgs.22.52 = MT 22:53) and the Baal-service provocation summary (web:1Kgs.22.53 = oshb:1Kgs.22.54 MT, the Masoretic book's final verse). The closing member of this reign stands in 2Kgs 1:17-18 beyond the book seam — the canonical division cuts a framework file in half, so this row closes with the book while its continuation is flagged as a cross-book relation, honoring the boundary without pretending the file is complete. Dual citation (+1) applies throughout.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Ahaziah's opening into Jehoshaphat's closing frame as the book's terminal miscellany — rejected because the synchronism formula unambiguously opens a new file in the framework grammar, and the canonical tiling requires the book's final rows to respect that grammar; the incompleteness belongs to the book division (Kings originally one scroll), not to the unit.
